title.zh: 卷八十四 列傳第三十四: 劉仁軌 郝處俊 裴行儉
title.en: Volume 84 Biographies 34: Liu Rengui, Hao Chujun, Pei Xingjian
title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第三十四: 劉仁軌 郝處俊 裴行儉 Volume 84 Biographies 34: Liu Rengui, Hao Chujun, Pei Xingjian

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌郝處俊裴行儉

translations.literal: Liu Rengui, Hao Chujun, and Pei Xingjian
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui, Hao Chujun, and Pei Xingjian

sentences.zh: （子光庭）

translations.literal: (His son Guangting)
translations.idiomatic: (His son Guangting)

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌，汴州尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui was a native of Weishi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui came from Weishi in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 少恭謹好學，遇隋末喪亂，不遑專習，每行坐所在，輒書空地，由是博涉文史。

translations.literal: In youth he was respectful, cautious, and fond of learning. When the chaos of disorder at the end of the Sui prevented him from devoting himself to study, wherever he walked or sat he would write on the bare ground, and thereby came to be broadly versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was dutiful and studious, but the turmoil at the end of the Sui left him no leisure for sustained study. Wherever he went, sitting or walking, he would trace characters on the ground, and in this way he gained a wide acquaintance with letters and history.

sentences.zh: 武德初，河南道大使、管國公任瑰將上表論事，仁軌見其起草，因為改定數字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Ren Gui, Grand Ambassador of the Henan Circuit and Duke of Guan, was about to submit a memorial discussing affairs. Rengui saw the draft and revised several characters for him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, Ren Gui, circuit ambassador for Henan and Duke of Guan, was preparing a policy memorial. Rengui saw the draft and corrected several phrases.

sentences.zh: 瑰甚異之，遂赤牒補息州參軍。

translations.literal: Ren Gui was greatly impressed and therefore had him appointed by red warrant as aide in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui was so struck by this that he had Rengui appointed military aide in Xizhou by special warrant.

sentences.zh: 稍除陳倉尉。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed assistant magistrate of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made assistant magistrate of Chencang.

sentences.zh: 部人有折衝都尉魯寧者，恃其高班，豪縱無禮，曆政莫能禁止。

translations.literal: Among those under his jurisdiction was the militia commander Lu Ning, who relied on his high rank, acted with arrogant license and without courtesy, and whom successive administrations had been unable to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: One man under his jurisdiction was the militia commander Lu Ning, who, relying on his senior rank, behaved with arrogant license and whom no previous magistrate had been able to control.

sentences.zh: 仁軌特加誡喻，期不可再犯，寧又暴橫尤甚，竟杖殺之。

translations.literal: Rengui gave him special admonition and warning, expecting that he would not offend again, but Ning became even more violent and overbearing, and in the end Rengui had him beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui admonished him sternly and warned that there must be no repeat offense, but Ning grew even more violent, and Rengui finally had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 州司以聞，太宗怒曰：“是何縣尉，輒殺吾折衝！”

translations.literal: The prefectural authorities reported this, and Emperor Taizong said in anger, "What sort of assistant magistrate is this, who dares kill my militia commander!"
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectural authorities reported the matter, Emperor Taizong flew into a rage. "What sort of assistant magistrate," he demanded, "dares kill one of my militia commanders!"

sentences.zh: 遽追入，與語，奇其剛正，擢授櫟陽丞。

translations.literal: He had him summoned at once and spoke with him, marveled at his firm uprightness, and promoted him to be assistant magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had Rengui summoned at once. After speaking with him and marveling at his firm integrity, he promoted him to assistant magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，太宗將幸同州校獵，屬收獲未畢，仁軌上表諫曰：“臣聞屋漏在上，知之者在下；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, when Emperor Taizong was about to go to Tong Prefecture for military hunting exercises, and the harvest was not yet complete, Rengui submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Your subject has heard that when the roof leaks above, those who know it are below;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 14, when Emperor Taizong was about to visit Tongzhou for a military hunt while the harvest was still unfinished, Rengui submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that when the roof leaks above, those who know it are below;

sentences.zh: 愚夫之計，擇之者聖人。

translations.literal: the plans of foolish men are chosen by sages.
translations.idiomatic: and that the plans of foolish men are chosen by sages.

sentences.zh: 是以周王詢於芻蕘，殷後謀於板築，故得享國彌久，傳祚無疆，功宣清廟，慶流後葉。

translations.literal: Therefore the King of Zhou inquired of grass cutters, and the ruler of Yin sought counsel from a wall-builder, and thus they were able to enjoy their states ever longer, transmit their thrones without limit, proclaim their merit in the clear temple, and extend their blessings to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the King of Zhou sought counsel from grass cutters and the ruler of Yin from a wall-builder, and so they prolonged their reigns, secured their succession, proclaimed their merit in the ancestral temple, and passed their blessings to later generations.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天性仁愛，躬親節儉，朝夕克念，百姓為心，一物失所，納隍軫慮。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is by nature benevolent and loving, personally practices economy, at morning and evening restrains your thoughts, takes the common people as your heart, and if a single thing is out of place, you grieve as though falling into a moat.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is by nature benevolent and loving, practices economy in person, and keeps the people always in mind; if even one creature is deprived, you grieve as though you had fallen into a moat.

sentences.zh: 臣伏聞大駕欲幸同州教習，臣伏知四時搜狩，前王恒典，事有沿革，未必因循。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the imperial carriage wishes to visit Tong Prefecture for training exercises. Your subject knows that the seasonal hunts of former kings were a constant institution, yet affairs have their changes and need not necessarily follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Your Majesty intends to visit Tongzhou for military exercises. I know that the seasonal hunts of former kings were a standing institution, yet circumstances change and precedent need not always be followed.

sentences.zh: 今年甘雨應時，秋稼極盛，玄黃亙野，十分才收一二；

translations.literal: This year timely sweet rains have fallen, the autumn crops are extremely abundant, black and yellow grain fill the fields, and only one or two parts in ten have been gathered;
translations.idiomatic: This year the rains came on time and the autumn harvest is abundant; black and yellow grain cover the fields, yet only one or two parts in ten have been gathered;

sentences.zh: 盡力刈獲，月半猶未訖功；

translations.literal: even with all their strength at reaping, after half a month the work is still not finished;
translations.idiomatic: even with every effort at reaping, after half a month the work is still not done;

sentences.zh: 貧家無力，禾下始擬種麥。

translations.literal: poor families lack strength, and only now beneath the standing grain do they plan to sow wheat.
translations.idiomatic: poor households lack the strength to do more, and only now beneath the standing grain are they planning to sow wheat.

sentences.zh: 直據尋常科喚，田家已有所妨。

translations.literal: according to the usual quotas for summons, farming households are already being hindered.
translations.idiomatic: Even the usual levies and summons already burden the farming households.

sentences.zh: 今既供承獵事，兼之修理橋道，縱大簡略，動費一二萬工，百姓收斂，實為狼狽。

translations.literal: Now that they must supply the hunting affair and in addition repair bridges and roads, even with great simplification this will require ten or twenty thousand laborers at a stroke, and the people's harvest will truly be thrown into distress.
translations.idiomatic: Now they must supply the hunt and also repair bridges and roads; even with every simplification, tens of thousands of laborers will be required at once, and the harvest will truly leave the people in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下少留萬乘之恩，垂聽一介之言，退近旬日，收刈總了，則人盡暇豫，家得康寧。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty would briefly withhold the grace of the imperial carriage, lend an ear to the words of a single man, and postpone for nearly ten days until the reaping is wholly finished; then the people will all have leisure and ease, and households will attain peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to withhold the imperial progress for a little while, heed the words of one humble subject, and delay for nearly ten days until the harvest is complete; then the people will have leisure and every household peace.

sentences.zh: 輿輪徐動，公私交泰。”

translations.literal: When the carriage wheels move slowly, public and private affairs will both prosper."
translations.idiomatic: When the wheels move at last, both public and private affairs will flourish together."

sentences.zh: 太宗特降璽書勞曰：“卿職任雖卑，竭誠奉國，所陳之事，朕甚嘉之。”

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong specially sent down an imperial letter of commendation, saying, "Though your office is low, you serve the state with full devotion; what you have set forth, We greatly commend."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent down a special imperial letter of commendation: "Though your post is humble, you serve the state with full devotion. What you have set forth, I greatly commend."

sentences.zh: 尋拜新安令，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed magistrate of Xin'an, and after repeated promotions became a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed magistrate of Xin'an and, after successive promotions, became supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 顯慶四年，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianqing he was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 4 he was appointed prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，高宗征遼，令仁軌監統水軍，以後期坐免，特令以白衣隨軍自效。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Emperor Gaozong campaigned against Liaodong, he ordered Rengui to supervise the navy, but because he arrived late he was dismissed from office and specially ordered to follow the army in plain clothes to redeem himself by service.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Emperor Gaozong campaigned against Liaodong, Rengui was placed in charge of the navy. He was dismissed for arriving late but was specially allowed to follow the army as a commoner and redeem himself by service.

sentences.zh: 時蘇定方既平百濟，留郎將劉仁願於百濟府城鎮守，又以左衛中郎將王文度為熊津都督，安撫其餘眾。

translations.literal: At that time Su Dingfang had already pacified Baekje and left the commandant Liu Renyuan to garrison the Baekje prefectural city, while appointing Wang Wendu, middle general of the Left Guard, as governor of Xiongjin to pacify the remaining population.
translations.idiomatic: By then Su Dingfang had pacified Baekje and left Commandant Liu Renyuan to garrison the Baekje capital, while appointing Wang Wendu of the Left Guard as governor of Xiongjin to pacify the remaining people.

sentences.zh: 文度濟海病卒。

translations.literal: Wendu crossed the sea and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu crossed the sea but died of illness on the way.

sentences.zh: 百濟為僧道琛、舊將福信率眾復叛，立故王子扶餘豐為王，引兵圍仁願於府城。

translations.literal: In Baekje the monk Dojun and the former general Fukushin led the masses in rebellion again, installed the former prince Buyeo Pung as king, and led troops to besiege Renyuan in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In Baekje the monk Dojun and the former general Fukushin raised a new rebellion, enthroned the former prince Buyeo Pung as king, and besieged Renyuan in the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 詔仁軌檢校帶方州刺史，代文度統眾，便道發新羅兵合勢以救仁願。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Rengui acting prefect of Daifang and ordered him to replace Wendu in command of the forces, and by the direct route to mobilize Silla troops and combine strength to rescue Renyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Daifang, replace Wendu in command, and by the direct route mobilize Silla troops to relieve Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 轉鬥而前，仁軌軍容整肅，所向皆下。

translations.literal: Fighting as he advanced, Rengui's army was orderly and stern in appearance, and wherever it went all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting as he advanced, Rengui kept his army in strict order, and every place he attacked fell.

sentences.zh: 道琛等乃釋仁願之圍，退保任存城。

translations.literal: Dojun and the others thereupon lifted the siege of Renyuan and withdrew to hold Jiren Castle.
translations.idiomatic: Dojun and his allies then lifted the siege of Renyuan and withdrew to Jiren Castle.

sentences.zh: 尋而福信殺道琛，並其兵馬，招誘亡叛，其勢益張。

translations.literal: Before long Fukushin killed Dojun and absorbed his troops and horses, recruited deserters and rebels, and his power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fukushin killed Dojun, absorbed his forces, and recruited deserters and rebels until his power grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 仁軌乃與仁願合軍休息。

translations.literal: Rengui then joined forces with Renyuan and rested the army.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui then united with Renyuan and gave the army a rest.

sentences.zh: 時蘇定方奉詔伐高麗，進圍平壤，不克而還。

translations.literal: At that time Su Dingfang, by imperial command, attacked Goguryeo, advanced to besiege Pyongyang, failed to take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Dingfang, by imperial command, attacked Goguryeo, besieged Pyongyang without success, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高宗敕書與仁軌曰：“平壤軍回，一城不可獨固，宜拔就新羅，共其屯守。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sent an imperial letter to Rengui, saying, "The Pyongyang army has returned; a single city cannot be held alone. You should withdraw to Silla and share garrison duty with them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong wrote to Rengui: "The Pyongyang army has withdrawn; one city cannot be held alone. You should pull out to Silla and share garrison duty there.

sentences.zh: 若金法敏藉卿等留鎮，宜且停彼；

translations.literal: If Kim Beopmin wishes you to remain and garrison there, you may stay for the time being;
translations.idiomatic: If Kim Beopmin asks you to remain and garrison the place, you may stay for the time being;

sentences.zh: 若其不須，即宜泛海還也。”

translations.literal: if he has no need of you, then you should cross the sea and return at once."
translations.idiomatic: if he does not need you, then you should cross the sea and return at once."

sentences.zh: 將士鹹欲西歸，仁軌曰：“《春秋》之義，大夫出疆，有可以安社稷、便國家、專之可也。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all wished to return west. Rengui said, "According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a grandee goes beyond the border, if there is something that can secure the altars of state and benefit the realm, he may act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers all wanted to return home. Rengui said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that when a minister goes beyond the border, if he can secure the altars of state and benefit the realm, he may act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 況在滄海之外，密邇豺狼者哉！

translations.literal: How much more when we are beyond the blue sea, close upon wolves and jackals!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when we are beyond the eastern sea, hard upon the enemy's lair!

sentences.zh: 且人臣進思盡忠，有死無貳，公家之利，知無不為。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a subject advances he should think of exhausting loyalty; there is death but no disloyalty; for the benefit of the public household, whatever he knows he must do.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a subject who advances should think only of exhausting his loyalty: death, but never disloyalty; for the state's benefit, whatever can be done must be done.

sentences.zh: 主上欲吞滅高麗，先誅百濟，留兵鎮守，製其心腹。

translations.literal: Our lord wishes to swallow and destroy Goguryeo, first executing Baekje, leaving troops to garrison and control its heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign wishes to destroy Goguryeo, and has first struck Baekje and left troops to garrison it and control its heartland.

sentences.zh: 雖妖孽充斥，而備預甚嚴，宜礪戈秣馬，擊其不意。

translations.literal: Although evil spirits fill the land, our preparations are very strict; we should sharpen our weapons and feed our horses and strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebels fill the land, our defenses are strong; we should sharpen our weapons, feed our horses, and strike where they do not expect us.

sentences.zh: 彼既無備，何攻不克？

translations.literal: Since they are unprepared, what attack will not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: If they are unprepared, what attack can fail?

sentences.zh: 戰而有勝，士卒自安。

translations.literal: If we fight and win, the soldiers will of themselves be reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Once we fight and win, the soldiers will regain their confidence.

sentences.zh: 然後分兵據險，開張形勢，飛表聞上，更請兵船。

translations.literal: Then we should divide the army to hold strategic points, display our power, send a swift memorial to inform the throne, and request more troops and ships.
translations.idiomatic: Then we can divide our forces to hold the passes, display our strength, send urgent dispatches to the throne, and request more troops and ships.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其有成，必當出師命將，聲援才接，凶逆自殲。

translations.literal: When the court knows that we have success, it will certainly dispatch armies and appoint generals; as soon as supporting forces arrive, the wicked rebels will destroy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sees that we are succeeding, it will surely send armies and appoint generals; as soon as reinforcements arrive, the rebels will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 非直不棄成功，實亦永清海外。

translations.literal: This is not only that we do not abandon success; in truth it will also forever pacify the lands beyond the sea.
translations.idiomatic: We would not only preserve what has been won; we would truly pacify the lands beyond the sea for good.

sentences.zh: 今平壤之軍既回，熊津又拔，則百濟餘燼，不日更興，高麗逋藪，何時可滅？

translations.literal: Now that the Pyongyang army has returned and Xiongjin has been withdrawn, the embers of Baekje will within days flare up again; when will the lair of Goguryeo ever be destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Pyongyang army has withdrawn and Xiongjin has been abandoned, the embers of Baekje will flare up again within days. When will Goguryeo ever be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 且今以一城之地，居賊中心，如其失腳，即為亡虜。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the territory of a single city we sit in the center of the enemy; if we lose our footing, we become captives at once.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with only one city we sit in the heart of the enemy; one misstep and we become prisoners.

sentences.zh: 拔入新羅，又是坐客，脫不如意，悔不可追。

translations.literal: If we withdraw into Silla, we again become guests sitting in another's house; if things do not go as we wish, regret cannot be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: If we withdraw into Silla, we become guests in another's house; if things go wrong, there will be no undoing it.

sentences.zh: 況福信凶暴，殘虐過甚，餘豐猜惑，外合內離，鴟張共處，勢必相害。

translations.literal: Moreover Fukushin is fierce and violent, his cruelty excessive; Pung is suspicious and unsettled; outwardly united but inwardly divided; like owls and hawks dwelling together, they are bound in the end to harm one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Fukushin is brutal and cruel beyond measure, while Pung is suspicious and divided within; like birds of prey caged together, they are bound to destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 唯宜堅守觀變，乘便取之，不可動也。”

translations.literal: We should only hold firm, watch for changes, and seize opportunity to take them; we must not move yet."
translations.idiomatic: We should hold firm, watch for changes, and strike when opportunity offers; we must not move yet."

sentences.zh: 眾從之。

translations.literal: The multitude followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The troops agreed.

sentences.zh: 時扶餘豐及福信等以真峴城臨江高險，又當衝要，加兵守之。

translations.literal: At that time Buyeo Pung and Fukushin and the others, because Jinsheng Castle stood by the river on high and dangerous ground and was also at a strategic point, added troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Pung and Fukushin then reinforced Jinsheng Castle, which stood on high ground above the river at a vital point.

sentences.zh: 仁軌引新羅之兵，乘夜薄城。

translations.literal: Rengui led Silla troops and by night pressed close to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui led Silla troops and under cover of night approached the city.

sentences.zh: 四面攀草而上，比明而入據其城，遂通新羅運糧之路。

translations.literal: On all four sides they climbed up by grasping the grass; by dawn they had entered and seized the city, and thereby opened the route by which Silla transported grain.
translations.idiomatic: On all sides they climbed the slopes by grasping the grass; by dawn they had taken the city and opened the Silla grain route.

sentences.zh: 俄而餘豐襲殺福信，又遣使往高麗及倭國請兵，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Before long Pung launched a surprise attack and killed Fukushin, and also sent envoys to Goguryeo and Wa to request troops to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pung killed Fukushin in a surprise attack and sent envoys to Goguryeo and Japan to request troops against the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 詔右威衛將軍孫仁師率兵浮海以為之援。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sun Renshi, general of the Right Majestic Guard, to lead troops across the sea as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi, general of the Right Majestic Guard, was ordered to lead troops across the sea as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 仁師既與仁軌等相合，兵士大振。

translations.literal: When Renshi had joined Rengui and the others, the soldiers were greatly heartened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Renshi joined Rengui, the army's morale soared.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將會議，或曰：“加林城水陸之衝，請先擊之。”

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals met in council, and some said, "Jialin Castle is the junction of land and water routes; please attack it first."
translations.idiomatic: The generals then met in council. Some said, "Jialin Castle commands both land and water routes; we should attack it first."

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：“加林險固，急攻則傷損戰士，固守則用日持久，不如先攻周留城。

translations.literal: Rengui said, "Jialin is perilous and strong; if we attack in haste we will injure and lose warriors, and if we besiege and hold it the days will drag on. It is better to attack Zhouliu Castle first.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui replied, "Jialin is strong and dangerous; a hasty assault will cost us men, and a siege will drag on. Better to attack Zhouliu first.

sentences.zh: 周留，賊之巢穴，群凶所聚，除惡務本，須拔其源。

translations.literal: Zhouliu is the rebels' lair, where all the villains gather; in removing evil one must strike at the root and pull up the source.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouliu is the rebels' lair where their leaders gather; to destroy evil one must strike at the root.

sentences.zh: 若克周留，則諸城自下。”

translations.literal: If we take Zhouliu, the other cities will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If we take Zhouliu, the other cities will fall of themselves."

sentences.zh: 於是仁師、仁願及新羅王金法敏帥陸軍以進。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renshi, Renyuan, and King Kim Beopmin of Silla led the land army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Renshi, Renyuan, and King Kim Beopmin of Silla then led the land army forward.

sentences.zh: 仁軌乃別率杜爽、扶餘隆率水軍及糧船，自熊津江往白江，會陸軍同趣周留城。

translations.literal: Rengui then separately led Du Shuang and Buyeo Yong with the navy and grain ships from the Xiongjin River toward the Ba River to join the land army in converging on Zhouliu Castle.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui separately led Du Shuang and Buyeo Yong with the navy and grain ships from the Xiongjin River to the Ba River to join the land army at Zhouliu.

sentences.zh: 仁軌遇倭兵於白江之口，四戰捷，焚其舟四百艘，煙焰漲天，海水皆赤，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: Rengui encountered Wa troops at the mouth of the Ba River, won four battles in succession, burned four hundred of their ships, smoke and flames filled the sky, the sea water all turned red, and the rebel masses were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At the mouth of the Ba River Rengui met the Japanese fleet, won four battles in succession, and burned four hundred ships until smoke filled the sky and the sea ran red; the enemy army broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 餘豐脫身而走，獲其寶劍。

translations.literal: Pung escaped with his body and fled; they captured his precious sword.
translations.idiomatic: Pung fled for his life, and they captured his ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 偽王子扶餘忠勝、忠誌等，率士女及倭眾並耽羅國使，一時並降。

translations.literal: The false princes Buyeo Chungsung, Chungji, and others led men and women together with Wa troops and envoys of Tamna, and all surrendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender princes Buyeo Chungsung and Chungji, together with men and women, Japanese troops, and envoys from Tamna, all surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 百濟諸城，皆復歸順。

translations.literal: All the cities of Baekje again returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: All the cities of Baekje submitted again.

sentences.zh: 賊帥遲受信據任存城不降。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Chi Suseung held Jiren Castle and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Chi Suseung held Jiren Castle and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 先是，百濟首領沙吒相如、黑齒常之自蘇定方軍回後，鳩集亡散，各據險以應福信，至是率其眾降。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Baekje leaders Shazha Xiangru and Heichi Changzhi, after Su Dingfang's army returned, had gathered the scattered and lost, each holding strategic points to respond to Fukushin; at this time they led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Su Dingfang's army withdrew, the Baekje leaders Shazha Xiangru and Heichi Changzhi had gathered scattered forces and held the passes in support of Fukushin; now they led their men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁軌諭以恩信，令自領子弟以取任存城，又欲分兵助之。

translations.literal: Rengui instructed them with favor and trust, ordered them to lead their own sons and younger brothers to take Jiren Castle, and also wished to divide troops to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui won them over with kindness and trust, ordered them to lead their own followers to take Jiren Castle, and offered to send troops to help.

sentences.zh: 孫仁師曰：“相如等獸心難信，若授以甲仗，是資寇兵也。”

translations.literal: Sun Renshi said, "Xiangru and the others have beast hearts and are hard to trust; if we give them armor and weapons, we are supplying the enemy's soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi objected, "Xiangru and the others have the hearts of beasts and cannot be trusted; if we arm them, we are arming the enemy."

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：“吾觀相如、常之皆忠勇有謀，感恩之士，從我則成，背我必滅，因機立效，在於茲日，不須疑也。”

translations.literal: Rengui said, "I observe that Xiangru and Changzhi are both loyal, brave, and resourceful, men who feel gratitude; if they follow us they will succeed, if they turn against us they will surely perish. To establish merit by seizing opportunity lies in this day; there is no need for doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Rengui replied, "In my view Xiangru and Changzhi are loyal, brave, and shrewd men who feel gratitude. If they follow us they will succeed; if they turn against us they will perish. This is the day for them to prove themselves; there is no need for doubt."

sentences.zh: 於是給其糧仗，分兵隨之，遂拔任存城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave them grain and weapons, divided troops to follow them, and thereby captured Jiren Castle.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them grain and arms, sent troops with them, and Jiren Castle was taken.

sentences.zh: 遲受信棄其妻子走投高麗，於是百濟之餘燼悉平。

translations.literal: Chi Suseung abandoned his wife and children and fled to Goguryeo, and thus the remaining embers of Baekje were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Suseung abandoned his family and fled to Goguryeo, and the last embers of Baekje were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 孫仁師與劉仁願振旅而還，詔留仁軌勒兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Sun Renshi and Liu Renyuan led the army back in good order; an edict left Rengui to command troops in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi and Liu Renyuan led the army home in good order, while Rengui was ordered to remain and garrison the territory.

sentences.zh: 初，百濟經福信之亂，合境凋殘，僵屍相屬。

translations.literal: At first, after the turmoil of Fukushin, all Baekje within its borders was wasted and desolate, corpses lying one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After Fukushin's rebellion, Baekje lay wasted throughout its borders, with corpses strewn one after another.

sentences.zh: 仁軌始令收斂骸骨，瘞埋吊祭之。

translations.literal: Rengui first ordered the gathering of bones and skeletons, burial in the ground, and mourning sacrifices for them.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui first ordered the dead gathered, buried, and mourned.

sentences.zh: 修錄戶口，署置官長，開通途路，整理村落，建立橋梁，補葺堤堰，修復陂塘，勸課耕種，賑貸貧乏，存問孤老。

translations.literal: He revised and recorded household registers, appointed officials and chiefs, opened thorough roads, put villages in order, built bridges, repaired dikes and dams, restored ponds and reservoirs, encouraged farming and cultivation, relieved and lent to the poor, and inquired after orphans and the aged.
translations.idiomatic: He registered households, appointed local officials, opened roads, restored villages, built bridges, repaired dikes and ponds, encouraged farming, relieved the poor, and cared for orphans and the aged.

sentences.zh: 頒宗廟忌諱，立皇家社稷。

translations.literal: He promulgated the taboos of the imperial ancestral temple and established the altars of the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the imperial ancestral taboos and established the royal altars of state.

sentences.zh: 百濟餘眾，各安其業。

translations.literal: The remaining people of Baekje each settled in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Baekje each returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 於是漸營屯田，積糧撫士，以經略高麗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gradually established military colonies, stored grain, comforted the soldiers, and planned strategy against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He then established military colonies, stored grain, comforted the troops, and prepared for operations against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 仁願既至京師，上謂曰：“卿在海東，前後奏請，皆合事宜，而雅有文理。

translations.literal: When Renyuan had reached the capital, the emperor said to him, "You were in the eastern sea; your memorials before and after were all suited to the circumstances, and moreover you have elegant literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: When Renyuan reached the capital, the emperor said to him, "In the east your memorials were always apt, and they are elegantly written besides.

sentences.zh: 卿本武將，何得然也？”

translations.literal: You are originally a military man; how could you be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a military man by training. How did you manage this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“劉仁軌之詞，非臣所及也。”

translations.literal: He replied, "Liu Rengui's words are not something your subject can match."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The words were Liu Rengui's, not mine."

sentences.zh: 上深歎賞之，因超加仁軌六階，正授帶方州刺史，並賜京城宅一區，厚賚其妻子，遣使降璽書勞勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply in admiration and therefore promoted Rengui by six ranks in extraordinary advancement, formally appointed him prefect of Daifang, and also granted him one residence in the capital, richly rewarded his wife and children, and sent an envoy with an imperial letter of commendation to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration, promoted Rengui six ranks in one leap, formally appointed him prefect of Daifang, granted him a residence in the capital, richly rewarded his family, and sent an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 仁軌又上表曰：

translations.literal: Rengui again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Rengui submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣蒙陛下曲垂天獎，棄瑕錄用，授之刺舉，又加連率。

translations.literal: Your subject has received Your Majesty's gracious heavenly favor bent low, been employed despite flaws, granted investigative authority, and further given command over allied forces.
translations.idiomatic: I have received Your Majesty's gracious favor, been employed despite my faults, given investigative authority, and placed in command of allied forces.

sentences.zh: 材輕職重，憂責更深，常思報效，冀酬萬一，智力淺短，淹滯無成。

translations.literal: My talent is light and my office heavy; my anxious responsibility is deeper still. I constantly think of repaying your favor and hope to requite even one part in ten thousand, yet my intelligence is shallow and short, and I linger without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: My talent is slight for so heavy an office, and my responsibility weighs on me all the more. I long to repay your favor even in the smallest measure, yet my abilities are limited and I have achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 久在海外，每從征役，軍旅之事，實有所聞。

translations.literal: Long abroad beyond the sea, I have repeatedly followed campaigns, and in military affairs I have truly gained some knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Long abroad, I have followed many campaigns and learned something of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 具狀封奏，伏願詳察。

translations.literal: I set forth the details in a sealed memorial and humbly wish that Your Majesty will examine it closely.
translations.idiomatic: I set forth the details in this sealed memorial and beg Your Majesty to examine them closely.

sentences.zh: 臣看見在兵募，手腳沉重者多，勇健奮發者少，兼有老弱，衣服單寒，唯望西歸，無心展效。

translations.literal: Your subject observes the soldiers now being recruited: many are heavy in hand and foot, few are brave, healthy, and eager; there are also old and weak among them, their clothing thin and cold; they only hope to return west and have no heart to display their merit.
translations.idiomatic: I see the men now being recruited: many are slow and heavy of limb, few are vigorous and eager; there are old and weak among them, poorly clothed, longing only to return home with no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 臣問：“往在海西，見百姓人人投募，爭欲征行，乃有不用官物，請自辦衣糧，投名義征。

translations.literal: Your subject asked, "In former days west of the sea, I saw common people all volunteering for recruitment, competing to go on campaign; some even refused government supplies and asked to provide their own clothing and grain, enrolling their names to serve in righteous expedition.
translations.idiomatic: I asked them, "In former days west of the sea I saw everyone volunteering for service, competing to join the campaign; some even refused government supplies and brought their own clothing and grain to enlist.

sentences.zh: 何因今日募兵，如此佇弱？”

translations.literal: Why is it that today's recruitment of soldiers is so feeble and weak?"
translations.idiomatic: Why are today's recruits so feeble and unwilling?"

sentences.zh: 皆報臣云：“ 今日官府，與往日不同，人心又別。

translations.literal: All replied to your subject, saying, "Today's government offices are not the same as in former days, and people's hearts are different as well.
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Today's government is not what it once was, and people's hearts have changed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽年中，東西征役，身死王事者，並蒙敕使吊祭，追贈官職，亦有回亡者官爵與其子弟。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui years, in eastern and western campaigns, those who died in the king's service all received imperial envoys for mourning sacrifices, posthumous grants of office, and there were also cases where those who returned from the dead had ranks and titles given to their sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, when men died on campaign east or west, imperial envoys mourned them, offices were granted posthumously, and even those reported dead who returned alive had ranks given to their sons.

sentences.zh: 從顯慶五年以後，征役身死，更不借問。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Xianqing onward, when men died on campaign, there was no further inquiry or concern.
translations.idiomatic: From Xianqing 5 onward, when men died on campaign, no one took notice.

sentences.zh: 往前渡遼海者，即得一轉勳官；

translations.literal: Those who previously crossed the Liao Sea would immediately receive one promotion in merit rank.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, anyone who crossed the Liao Sea could earn a step up in merit rank.

sentences.zh: 從顯慶五年以後，頻經渡海，不被記錄。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Xianqing onward, though men crossed the sea again and again, it was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: But from Xianqing 5 on, men who crossed the sea repeatedly went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 州縣發遣兵募，人身少壯、家有錢財、參逐官府者，東西藏避，並即得脫；

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties dispatched conscripts, those who were young and strong, had wealth at home, and could attend upon the government offices hid east and west and all immediately escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the counties sent out conscripts, the young and strong who had money and knew how to deal with officials could dodge here and there and slip free.

sentences.zh: 無錢參逐者，雖是老弱，推背即來。

translations.literal: Those without money to attend upon the offices, even if old and weak, came as soon as they were pushed from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not bribe their way through were dragged in—old or weak, they came at a shove.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，破百濟勳，及向平壤苦戰勳，當時軍將號令，並言與高官重賞，百方購募，無種不道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, for merit in breaking Baekje and for merit in bitter fighting toward Pyongyang, the army generals' orders at that time all spoke of high office and heavy reward, buying and recruiting in a hundred ways, saying everything imaginable.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 5, when rewards were promised for crushing Baekje and for the bloody fighting toward Pyongyang, the generals' calls promised high rank and rich bounty, soliciting recruits by every means imaginable.

sentences.zh: 洎到西岸，唯聞枷鎖推禁，奪賜破勳，州縣追呼，求住不得，公私困弊，不可言盡。

translations.literal: By the time they reached the western shore, they heard only of cangues and shackles forcing confinement, stripped rewards and voided merit, prefectures and counties chasing and summoning them, seeking rest but unable to obtain it; public and private distress cannot be fully told.
translations.idiomatic: But once they reached the western shore, they found only chains and forced detention, stolen rewards and denied merit, endless summons from local officials with no respite—public and private misery beyond words.

sentences.zh: 發海西之日，已有自害逃走，非獨海外始逃。

translations.literal: On the day they were sent west across the sea, some already harmed themselves and fled; flight did not begin only after reaching overseas.
translations.idiomatic: Some men already killed themselves or fled on the day they were sent west across the sea; flight did not begin only after they reached overseas.

sentences.zh: 又為征役，蒙授勳級，將為榮寵，頻年征役，唯取勳官，牽挽辛苦，與白丁無別。

translations.literal: Again serving in campaigns, they received merit grades and took it for honor and favor; yet year after year of campaigning brought only merit titles, dragged about in hardship no different from common conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Men might have thought campaign service would bring merit rank and honor, but after years of conscription they received only hollow merit titles while suffering the same drudgery as any ordinary soldier.

sentences.zh: 百姓不願征行，特由於此。”

translations.literal: The common people are unwilling to go on campaign—it is especially because of this.
translations.idiomatic: This, above all, is why the people refuse to march to war.

sentences.zh: 陛下再興兵馬，平定百濟，留兵鎮守，經略高麗。

translations.literal: Your Majesty again raised armies and horses, pacified Baekje, left troops to garrison and defend, and planned to advance against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised armies again, crushed Baekje, stationed troops to hold the land, and set out to subdue Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 百姓有如此議論，若為成就功業？

translations.literal: The common people have such talk—how can great achievements be accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: When the people talk like this, how can you finish what you have begun?

sentences.zh: 臣聞琴瑟不調，改而更張，布政施化，隨時取適。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the qin and se are out of tune, one removes and restrings them; in spreading governance and applying transformation, one adapts to the times.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the harp and lute are out of tune, one must restring them; in governing, policy must suit the hour.

sentences.zh: 自非重賞明罰，何以成功？

translations.literal: Unless there are heavy rewards and clear punishments, how can success be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Without generous rewards and stern punishments, how can you succeed?

sentences.zh: 臣又問：“見在兵募，舊留鎮五年，尚得支濟；

translations.literal: I also asked: 'The conscripts now present—those who formerly garrisoned for five years still had enough to sustain themselves;
translations.idiomatic: I also asked, 'The men now under arms who used to garrison for five years still managed to get by;

sentences.zh: 爾等始經一年，何因如此單露？”

translations.literal: you have been through only one year—why are you so thinly clad?'
translations.idiomatic: you have served only one year—why are you so poorly clothed?'

sentences.zh: 並報臣道：“發家來日，唯遣作一年裝束，自從離家，已經二年。

translations.literal: They all replied to me: 'From the day we left home, we were sent with provision for only one year's outfit; since leaving home, already two years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: They all told me, 'When we left home we were given supplies for only one year, yet we have been away for two years already.

sentences.zh: 在朝陽甕津，又遣來去運糧，涉海遭風，多有漂失。”

translations.literal: At Chaoyang and Ungjin we were again sent back and forth to transport grain; crossing the sea we met wind, and many were washed away and lost.'
translations.idiomatic: At Chaoyang and Ungjin we were sent shuttling grain; crossing the sea we met storms, and many perished.'

sentences.zh: 臣勘責見在兵募，衣裳單露，不堪度冬者，給大軍還日所留衣裳，且得一冬充事。

translations.literal: I examined the conscripts now present; for those whose clothes were thin and exposed and who could not endure the winter, I gave the clothes left when the great army returned, so they could manage for one winter.
translations.idiomatic: I found men too lightly clothed to survive the winter and issued them garments left behind when the main army withdrew, enough to last one winter.

sentences.zh: 來年秋後，更無準擬。

translations.literal: After next autumn, there is no further provision planned.
translations.idiomatic: After next autumn, there is nothing further set aside for them.

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲殄滅高麗，不可棄百濟土地。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to destroy and extinguish Goguryeo, you cannot abandon Baekje territory.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty means to destroy Goguryeo, you cannot abandon Baekje's lands.

sentences.zh: 餘豐在北，餘勇在南，百濟、高麗，舊相黨援，倭人雖遠，亦相影響，若無兵馬，還成一國。

translations.literal: Yu Feng is in the north and Yu Yong in the south; Baekje and Goguryeo of old mutually aided as allies; though the Wo people are distant, they also influence each other—without troops and horses, they would again become one state.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Feng in the north and Yu Yong in the south, Baekje and Goguryeo have long been allies; though Wa lies far away, they sway one another—without our armies, they would reunite as one kingdom.

sentences.zh: 既須鎮壓，又置屯田，事藉兵士，同心同德。

translations.literal: One must both suppress by garrison and establish military colonies; the affair depends on soldiers of one heart and one virtue.
translations.idiomatic: You must garrison and farm the land alike; the work depends on soldiers who stand together.

sentences.zh: 兵士既有此議，不可膠柱因循，須還其渡海官勳及平百濟向平壤功效。

translations.literal: Since the soldiers already have such talk, one cannot stick to the pillar and follow old ways—one must restore to them their official merit for crossing the sea and their achievements in breaking Baekje and advancing toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers already speak of these grievances; you must not cling stubbornly to the old course—you should restore their merit ranks for crossing the sea and their rewards for crushing Baekje and fighting toward Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 除此之外，更相褒賞，明敕慰勞，以起兵募之心。

translations.literal: Beyond this, further mutual praise and reward, clear edicts to comfort and commend, to stir the hearts of those raising conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, grant further honors, issue clear orders of thanks and encouragement, and win back the will to serve.

sentences.zh: 若依今日以前布置，臣恐師老且疲，無所成就。

translations.literal: If one follows arrangements as before today, I fear the army will grow old and weary, accomplishing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If you keep to the present arrangements, I fear the army will tire and achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣又見晉代平吳，史籍具載。

translations.literal: I have also seen the Jin dynasty's pacification of Wu—the histories fully record it.
translations.idiomatic: I have read what the histories tell of how Jin conquered Wu.

sentences.zh: 內有武帝、張華，外有羊祜、杜預，籌謀策畫，經緯諮詢。

translations.literal: Within were Emperor Wu and Zhang Hua; outside were Yang Hu and Du Yu—planning strategies and weaving counsels in consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court were Emperor Wu and Zhang Hua; in the field were Yang Hu and Du Yu—all plotting together in counsel.

sentences.zh: 王浚之徒，折衝萬里，樓船戰艦，已到石頭。

translations.literal: Wang Jun and his kind, breaking the enemy charge for ten thousand li—tower ships and war vessels had already reached Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and his fellows had fought ten thousand li; their tower ships already stood at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 賈充、王渾之輩，猶欲斬張華以謝天下。

translations.literal: Jia Chong, Wang Hun, and their sort still wished to behead Zhang Hua to appease all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Chong, Wang Hun, and men like them still wanted Zhang Hua's head to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 武帝報云：“平吳之計，出自朕意，張華同朕見耳，非其本心。”

translations.literal: Emperor Wu replied: 'The plan to pacify Wu came from my intent; Zhang Hua shared my view—that is all, not his own original design.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu answered, 'The plan to conquer Wu came from me; Zhang Hua merely shared my view—it was not his scheme alone.'

sentences.zh: 是非不同，乖亂如此。

translations.literal: Right and wrong were not the same; disorder and confusion were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Even on right and wrong they could not agree; the court was torn like this.

sentences.zh: 平吳之後，猶欲苦繩王浚，賴武帝擁護，始得保全。

translations.literal: After pacifying Wu, they still wished to harshly bind Wang Jun with the law; thanks to Emperor Wu's protection, he was at last preserved.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, they still tried to bring Wang Jun to harsh account; only Emperor Wu's protection saved him.

sentences.zh: 不逢武帝聖明，王浚不存首領。

translations.literal: Had he not met Emperor Wu's sagely clarity, Wang Jun would not have kept his head.
translations.idiomatic: Without Emperor Wu's wisdom, Wang Jun would have lost his life.

sentences.zh: 臣每讀其書，未嚐不撫心長歎。

translations.literal: Each time I read those records, never once did I not press my heart and sigh long.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read those pages, I cannot help but sigh from the depths of my heart.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下既得百濟，欲取高麗，須外內同心，上下齊奮，舉無遺策，始可成功。

translations.literal: Humbly considering: Your Majesty having already obtained Baekje and wishing to take Goguryeo, one must have inner and outer of one heart, upper and lower striving together, every move without missed strategy—only then can success be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has taken Baekje and aims at Goguryeo; you need the court and the field of one mind, high and low striving as one, every measure well laid—only then can you succeed.

sentences.zh: 百姓既有此議，更宜改調。

translations.literal: Since the common people already have such talk, it is all the more fitting to change the tune.
translations.idiomatic: The people already murmur thus; you should change course all the more.

sentences.zh: 臣恐是逆耳之事，無人為陛下盡言。

translations.literal: I fear these are things harsh to the ear; no one speaks fully to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear such unwelcome truths go unsaid to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 自顧老病日侵，殘生詎幾？

translations.literal: Reflecting on myself, old age and illness daily encroach—how much remains of this feeble life?
translations.idiomatic: I am old and ill, and my days are few.

sentences.zh: 奄忽長逝，銜恨九泉，所以披露肝膽，昧死聞奏。

translations.literal: Should I suddenly pass away, I would bear resentment in the Nine Springs; therefore I lay bare my liver and gall and risk death to report to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Should I die soon, I would carry regret to the grave; therefore I lay bare my heart and risk my life to speak before you.

sentences.zh: 上深納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took his counsel deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 又遣劉仁願率兵渡海，與舊鎮兵交代，仍授扶餘隆熊津都督，遣以招輯其餘眾。

translations.literal: He also sent Liu Rengyuan to lead troops across the sea to relieve the old garrison troops, appointed Buyeo Rong Commander of Ungjin, and dispatched him to summon and gather the remaining multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent Liu Rengyuan across the sea with troops to relieve the old garrison, appointed Buyeo Rong commander of Ungjin, and charged him with rallying the remaining loyalists.

sentences.zh: 扶餘勇者，扶餘隆之弟也，是時走在倭國，以為扶餘豐之應，故仁軌表言之。

translations.literal: Buyeo Yongzhe was Buyeo Rong's younger brother; at this time he had fled to the Wo country and was regarded as the counterpart to Buyeo Feng—therefore Rengui memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Yongzhe, younger brother of Buyeo Rong, had fled to Wa and was regarded as a rallying point for Buyeo Feng's faction; Rengui reported this in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 於是仁軌浮海西還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rengui floated across the western sea and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Then Rengui sailed west across the sea and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，仁軌將發帶方州，謂人曰：“天將富貴此翁耳！”

translations.literal: Initially, when Rengui was about to depart from Daifang Province, he said to people: 'Heaven is about to enrich and ennoble this old man!'
translations.idiomatic: When Rengui was about to leave Daifang Province, he told others, 'Heaven will soon make this old man rich and honored!'

sentences.zh: 於州司請曆日一卷，並七廟諱，人怪其故，答曰：“擬削平遼海，頒示國家正朔，使夷俗遵奉焉。”

translations.literal: At the provincial office he requested one scroll of the calendar and the taboo names of the Seven Temples; people wondered at the reason, and he replied: 'I intend to cut down and pacify the Liao Sea, proclaim the state's correct calendar, and make barbarian customs observe it.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked the provincial office for a calendar scroll and the imperial taboo names; when people wondered why, he said, 'I mean to pacify the lands beyond the sea, impose our calendar, and make those barbarian ways bow to it.'

sentences.zh: 至是皆如其言。

translations.literal: At this time, all came about as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: And so it all came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年，封泰山，仁軌領新羅及百濟、耽羅、倭四國酋長赴會，高宗甚悅，擢拜大司憲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longde, at the Fengshan rite on Mount Tai, Rengui led the chieftains of Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Wo of the four states to attend; Gaozong was greatly pleased and promoted him to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Longde 2, at the Mount Tai rite, Rengui led chieftains from Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Wa; Gaozong was delighted and made him Grand Censor of State.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，遷右相，兼檢校太子左中護，累前後戰功，封樂城縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, he was transferred to Right Chancellor, concurrently Acting Left Central Guard of the Crown Prince; accumulating his successive battle achievements, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lecheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng 1 he became Right Chancellor and acting Left Central Guard of the Crown Prince; for his accumulated victories he was enfeoffed Baron of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，為熊津道安撫大使，兼浿江道總管，副司空李勣討平高麗。

translations.literal: In the third year, he served as Pacification Commissioner of the Ungjin Circuit and concurrently Commander of the Paek River Circuit, assisting Minister of Works Li Ji in campaigning to pacify Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was Pacification Commissioner of the Ungjin Circuit and commander of the Paek River Circuit, serving under Li Ji in the conquest of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，軍回，以疾辭職，加金紫光祿大夫，聽致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang, the army returned; he resigned due to illness, was given the title of Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang 2, after the army returned, he resigned on grounds of illness, was granted Golden Seal and Purple Girdle Grand Master, and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，復授隴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, he was again appointed Prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 he was again made Prefect of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，征拜太子左庶子、同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervising the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, given third rank at court, and charged with supervising the national history.

sentences.zh: 五年，為雞林道大總管，東伐新羅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was Grand Commander of the Jilin Circuit, campaigning east to attack Silla.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he became Grand Commander of the Jilin Circuit and marched east against Silla.

sentences.zh: 仁軌率兵徑度瓠盧河，破其北方大鎮七重城。

translations.literal: Rengui led troops directly crossing the Hulu River and broke their great northern fortress, Sevenfold City.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui led his army straight across the Hulu River and seized their great northern stronghold, Sevenfold Wall.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公，並子侄三人，並授上柱國。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced in rank to Duke; together with three sons and nephews, all were granted Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was raised to duke; three sons and nephews were also made Senior Pillars of State.

sentences.zh: 州黨榮之，號其所居為樂城鄉三柱裏。

translations.literal: The clans of the prefecture honored this and called the place where they dwelt 'Three-Pillar Lane of Lecheng Township.'
translations.idiomatic: His home district took pride in this and called his neighborhood Three-Pillar Lane in Lecheng Township.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，拜尚書左僕射、同中書門下三品，兼太子賓客，依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Same Rank as the Three Offices, concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince, continuing to supervise the national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with third rank at court, concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince, and continued to oversee the national history.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，以吐蕃入寇，命仁軌為洮河道行軍鎮守大使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, because Tibet invaded, Rengui was appointed Mobile Pacification Commissioner of the Taohe Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng 2, when Tibet raided the frontier, Rengui was made field commander and garrison commissioner on the Taohe River.

sentences.zh: 仁軌每有奏請，多被中書令李敬玄抑之，由是與敬玄不協。

translations.literal: Whenever Rengui had memorial requests, many were suppressed by Secretariat Director Li Jingxuan; because of this he was not in harmony with Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui found many of his memorials blocked by Chief Minister Li Jingxuan, and the two grew estranged.

sentences.zh: 仁軌知敬玄素非邊將才，冀欲中傷之，上言西蕃鎮守事非敬玄莫可。

translations.literal: Rengui knew Jingxuan had never been a frontier general by nature and hoped to harm him; he memorialized that for garrisoning against the western Tibetans, no one but Jingxuan would do.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Jingxuan was no frontier commander, Rengui sought to undermine him and declared that only Jingxuan could hold the western garrison against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 高宗遽命敬玄代之。

translations.literal: Gaozong hurriedly ordered Jingxuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong promptly ordered Jingxuan to take his place.

sentences.zh: 敬玄至洮河軍，尋為吐蕃所敗。

translations.literal: Jingxuan reached the Taohe Army and was soon defeated by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan reached the Taohe garrison and was soon beaten by the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, he was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong 2 he also became Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以老乞骸骨，聽解尚書左僕射，以太子太傅依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Before long, citing old age he requested to retire; permitted to relinquish Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, he continued to manage state affairs as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire on account of age; allowed to step down as Left Vice Director, he continued in government as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，高宗幸東都，皇太子京師監國，遣仁軌與侍中裴炎、中書令薛元超留輔太子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Gaozong visited the Eastern Capital; the Crown Prince watched over the state in the capital; Rengui was sent with Palace Attendant Pei Yan and Secretariat Director Xue Yuanchao to remain and assist the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun 1, when Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital and the Crown Prince remained in Chang'an as regent, Rengui was left with Pei Yan and Xue Yuanchao to assist him.

sentences.zh: 二年，太子赴東都，又令太孫重照京師留守，仍令仁軌為副。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Crown Prince went to the Eastern Capital; the Imperial Grandson Zhongzhao was again left to hold the capital; Rengui was again made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, when the Crown Prince went east, Imperial Grandson Zhongzhao was left in Chang'an and Rengui again served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，加授特進，復拜尚書左僕射、同中書門下三品，專知留守事。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, he was additionally granted Special Advancement, again appointed Left Vice Director with third rank, and charged solely with managing the capital regency.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took the regency, she granted him Special Advancement, again made him Left Vice Director with third rank, and put him in sole charge of the capital regency.

sentences.zh: 仁軌復上疏辭以衰老，請罷居守之任，因陳呂後禍敗之事，以申規諫。

translations.literal: Rengui again submitted a memorial declining on grounds of age, asking to be relieved of the regency post, and citing the calamitous fall of Empress Lü as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui memorialized again, pleading age and asking to be released from the regency, citing the ruin brought by Empress Lü as a warning.

sentences.zh: 則天使武承嗣齎璽書往京慰喻之曰：“今日以皇帝諒暗不言，眇身且代親政。

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent Wu Chengsi bearing an imperial sealed letter to the capital to comfort and instruct him, saying: 'Today, because the Emperor remains in mourning seclusion and does not speak, I myself for the moment act in his stead in personal governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian sent Wu Chengsi to Chang'an with an imperial letter of consolation, saying, 'The Emperor is in mourning and cannot speak; I govern in his place for now.

sentences.zh: 遠勞勸誡，復表辭衰疾，怪望既多，徊徨失據。

translations.literal: You have troubled yourself from afar with admonition; again you memorialized declining due to debility and illness—my astonishment and expectations are many; I am hesitant and without footing.
translations.idiomatic: Your far counsel moves me, yet you again plead illness—I am both astonished and troubled, uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 又雲‘呂後見嗤於後代，祿、產貽禍於漢朝’，引喻良深，愧慰交集。

translations.literal: You also said, "Empress Lü was mocked by later generations; Lu and Chan brought calamity to the Han dynasty"—the allusion is very deep; shame and comfort intermingle.
translations.idiomatic: When you cite Empress Lü's shame in later ages and the disaster Lu and Chan brought upon Han—the analogy cuts deep, and I feel both reproach and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 公忠貞之操，終始不渝；

translations.literal: Your loyal and steadfast character, from beginning to end unchanging;
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty has never wavered;

sentences.zh: 勁直之風，古今罕比。

translations.literal: your forceful straightness of manner is rarely matched in past or present.
translations.idiomatic: your uncompromising integrity is seldom matched in any age.

sentences.zh: 初聞此語，能不罔然；

translations.literal: At first hearing these words, one cannot but be unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: At first I was shaken to hear it;

sentences.zh: 靜而思之，是為龜鏡。

translations.literal: but reflecting quietly, it serves as a mirror and oracle.
translations.idiomatic: yet on reflection I see it as a mirror for my own conduct.

sentences.zh: 且端揆之任，儀刑百辟，況公先朝舊德，遐邇具瞻。

translations.literal: Moreover, the charge of chief minister models all officials—how much more so for you, an elder virtue of the former court, looked to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister you set the example for all officials, and as an elder statesman of the prior reign, the realm looks to you.

sentences.zh: 願以匡救為懷，無以暮年致請。”

translations.literal: I hope you will take correcting and saving as your heart's aim, and not use advancing years to make your request.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask you to govern in the spirit of loyal counsel, and not to insist on retirement in your old age.'

sentences.zh: 尋進封郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to full duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，從新令改為文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong, following the new ordinance he was changed to Left Minister of the Palace Secretariat, Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 1, under the new titles he became Left Minister of the Palace Secretariat with third rank at court.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年八十四。

translations.literal: Soon he passed away, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 則天廢朝三日，令在京百官以次赴吊，冊贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，賜其家實封三百戶。

translations.literal: Empress Wu suspended court for three days, ordered all officials in the capital to go in turn to mourn, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master of Honor with Ceremony equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and Grand Governor of Bing Prefecture, granted burial at Qianling, and gave his family three hundred households of actual enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian halted court for three days and ordered the capital officials to mourn in turn; posthumously she enfeoffed him Grand Master of Honor with Ceremony equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and Grand Governor of Bingzhou, granted burial at Qianling, and gave his household three hundred tax households.

sentences.zh: 仁軌雖位居端揆，不自矜倨。

translations.literal: Though Rengui's rank was chief minister, he did not pride himself or act haughty.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rengui stood at the pinnacle of office, he never grew proud.

sentences.zh: 每見貧賤時故人，不改布衣之舊。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw old acquaintances from his days of poverty and low rank, he did not change his former plain-cloth ways.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met old friends from his poor days, he still treated them as he had in common clothes.

sentences.zh: 初為陳倉尉，相工袁天綱謂曰：“君終當位鄰台輔，年將九十。”

translations.literal: When he first served as Chencang District Captain, the physiognomist Yuan Tiangang said to him: 'Sir will ultimately attain rank neighboring the chief ministers, and your years will approach ninety.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was a clerk at Chencang, the physiognomist Yuan Tiangang told him, 'You will rise to the very threshold of the chief ministers, and live nearly ninety years.'

sentences.zh: 後果如其言。

translations.literal: Later it truly came about as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 仁軌身經隋末之亂，輯其見聞，著《行年記》，行於代。

translations.literal: Rengui personally lived through the chaos at the end of Sui; he compiled what he had seen and heard and authored the Record of the Journey of Years, which circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui lived through the chaos at the end of Sui, gathered what he had seen and heard, and wrote the Record of Years, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子浚，官至太子中舍人。

translations.literal: His son Jun reached the office of Middle Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun rose to Middle Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，為酷吏所陷，被殺，妻子籍沒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, he was framed by cruel officials, was killed, and his wife and children were confiscated and registered as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 2 cruel officials framed him; he was executed, and his wife and children were seized.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以仁軌春宮舊僚，追贈太尉。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, because Rengui had been an old colleague in the Eastern Palace, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, he posthumously made Rengui Grand Marshal in remembrance of their days in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 浚子冕，開元中，為秘書省少監，表請為仁軌立碑，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: Jun's son Mian, in the Kaiyuan era, served as Vice Director of the Secretariat; he memorialized requesting a stele be erected for Rengui, with posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's grandson Mian, Vice Director of the Secretariat in the Kaiyuan era, petitioned for a stele to Rengui and gave him the posthumous title Literary Offering.

sentences.zh: 史臣韋述曰：世稱劉樂城與戴至德同為端揆，劉則甘言接人，以收物譽；

translations.literal: Historian Wei Shu said: The world says Liu Lecheng and Dai Zhide were both chief ministers—Liu with sweet words received people to gather worldly praise;
translations.idiomatic: The historian Wei Shu wrote: People say Liu Lecheng and Dai Zhide both held the chief ministership; Liu won favor with pleasant words and courted reputation.

sentences.zh: 戴則正色拒下，推美於君。

translations.literal: Dai with stern countenance rejected those below and pushed merit to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Dai kept a stern face toward subordinates and credited merit to the throne.

sentences.zh: 故樂城之善於今未弭，而戴氏之勣無所聞焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Lecheng's praise in the present has not ceased, while Dai's achievements are nowhere heard of.
translations.idiomatic: So Liu's renown still lingers, while Dai's accomplishments go unspoken.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 高名美稱，或因邀飾而致遠；

translations.literal: High renown and fine titles may, through eager adornment, reach far;
translations.idiomatic: Great fame and flattering praise may travel far because men polish their reputations;

sentences.zh: 深仁至行，或以韜晦而莫傳。

translations.literal: deep benevolence and utmost conduct may, through hiding their light, go untransmitted.
translations.idiomatic: while deep virtue and true devotion may never be known because men hide their light.

sentences.zh: 豈唯劉、戴而然，蓋自古有之矣。

translations.literal: Is it only Liu and Dai who are thus? From antiquity there have been such cases.
translations.idiomatic: This is not true of Liu and Dai alone—it has been so since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：“眾好之，必察焉；

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: 'What the multitude likes—one must examine it;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Confucius said, 'What all men praise, examine closely;

sentences.zh: 眾惡之，必察焉。”

translations.literal: what the multitude hates—one must examine it.'
translations.idiomatic: what all men condemn, examine closely.'

sentences.zh: 非夫聖智，鮮不惑也。

translations.literal: Without sage wisdom, few are not bewildered.
translations.idiomatic: Without the wisdom of a sage, few escape confusion.

sentences.zh: 且劉公逞其私忿，陷人之所不能，覆徒貽國之恥，忠恕之道，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, Lord Liu indulged his private resentment, entrapped people beyond what could be done, and in the end only brought shame on the state—is this what the way of loyalty and forbearance is?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Liu Rengui gave rein to private resentment, pressed charges beyond what justice allowed, and in the end only shamed the realm—can this be the way of loyalty and forbearance?

sentences.zh: 郝處俊，安州安陸人也。

translations.literal: Hao Chujun was a native of Anlu in Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chujun was a native of Anlu in Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 父相貴，隋末，與妻父許紹據硤州歸國，以功授滁州刺史，封甑山縣公。

translations.literal: His father Xiang Gui, at the end of Sui, together with his wife's father Xu Shao held Xia Prefecture and submitted to the Tang; for merit he was appointed Prefect of Chuzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zenshan County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang Gui; at the end of the Sui, he and his father-in-law Xu Shao held Xia Prefecture and submitted to the Tang. For his service he became Prefect of Chuzhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zenshan County.

sentences.zh: 處俊年十歲餘，其父卒於滁州，父之故吏賻送甚厚，僅滿千餘匹，悉辭不受。

translations.literal: Chujun was a little over ten when his father died at Chuzhou; his father's former subordinates sent lavish condolence gifts, totaling more than a thousand bolts of silk, all of which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was barely ten when his father died at Chuzhou. His father's former officials sent lavish funeral gifts—over a thousand bolts of silk in all—and he refused every one.

sentences.zh: 及長，好讀《漢書》，略能暗誦。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved reading the Book of Han and could recite much of it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he loved the Book of Han and could recite much of it by heart.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，本州進士舉，吏部尚書高士廉甚奇之，解褐授著作佐郎，襲爵甑山縣公。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, he passed the provincial jinshi examination; Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian greatly admired him, and he left commoner status to become Assistant Editorial Director, inheriting the title Duke of Zenshan County.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he passed the provincial jinshi examination. Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian took great notice of him; he entered office as Assistant Editorial Director and inherited the title Duke of Zenshan County.

sentences.zh: 兄弟篤睦，事諸舅甚謹。

translations.literal: He and his brothers were deeply harmonious and served their maternal uncles with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brothers were deeply close and served their maternal uncles with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 再轉滕王友，恥為王官，遂棄官歸耕。

translations.literal: After two transfers he became Companion to the Prince of Teng; ashamed to be a prince's retainer, he resigned and returned to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred twice, he became a Companion to the Prince of Teng; ashamed to serve as a prince's retainer, he resigned and returned to the fields.

sentences.zh: 久之，召拜太子司議郎，五遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Palace Gentleman for Discussion in the Heir Apparent's Household; after five promotions he became Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was summoned as Palace Gentleman for Discussion in the Heir Apparent's Household; after five promotions he reached Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，改為司列少常伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was changed to Assistant Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfeng he became Assistant Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 屬高麗反叛，詔司空李勣為浿江道大總管，以處俊為副。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo rebelled, an edict made Minister of Works Li Ji Grand Commander of the Paekchon River Circuit, with Chujun as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo rebelled, Li Ji was made Grand Commander of the Paekchon River Circuit and Chujun his deputy.

sentences.zh: 嚐次賊城，未遑置陣，賊徒奄至，軍中大駭。

translations.literal: Once when camped near an enemy city, before arrays could be set, enemy troops suddenly arrived and the army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while encamped near an enemy city before battle lines could be formed, enemy troops rushed in and the army panicked.

sentences.zh: 處俊獨據胡床，方餐乾糧，乃潛簡精銳擊敗之，將士多服其膽略。

translations.literal: Chujun alone sat on a camp stool, still eating dry rations; he secretly selected crack troops and defeated them—the officers and men greatly admired his courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun alone sat on a folding stool, still eating dry rations; he quietly picked elite troops and routed the enemy, and the officers and men admired his nerve and foresight.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，拜東台侍郎，尋同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang he was appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace; soon he served concurrently as Third Rank of Both Eastern and Western Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zongzhang he became Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace and soon held Third Rank at both Eastern and Western Terraces.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，高宗幸東都，皇太子於京師監國，盡留侍臣戴至德、張文瓘等以輔太子，獨以處俊從。

translations.literal: At the start of Xianheng, Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital; the Crown Prince remained at the capital to oversee the realm. All attendant ministers such as Dai Zhide and Zhang Wenguan were left to assist the Prince; only Chujun accompanied the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianheng the Emperor went to the Eastern Capital while the Crown Prince stayed at Chang'an as regent. All the attendant ministers—Dai Zhide, Zhang Wenguan, and the rest—were left with the Prince; only Chujun went with the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時東州道總管高侃破高麗餘眾於安市城，奏稱有高麗僧言中國災異，請誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Circuit Commander Gao Kan of the East Circuit Route defeated Goguryeo remnants at Anshi City and memorialized that a Goguryeo monk spoke of calamities and omens in China, requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Route Commander Gao Kan defeated Goguryeo remnants at Anshi and reported that a Goguryeo monk had spoken of calamities in China; execution was requested.

sentences.zh: 上謂處俊曰：“朕聞為君上者，以天下之目而視，以天下之耳而聽，蓋欲廣聞見也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Chujun: "I have heard that a ruler views with the eyes of all under Heaven and listens with the ears of all under Heaven—this is to broaden what he sees and hears.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Chujun: "A ruler, I hear, should see with the eyes of the empire and hear with its ears—to widen his knowledge.

sentences.zh: 且天降災異，所以警悟人君。

translations.literal: Moreover, Heaven sends calamities and omens to awaken and enlighten rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends calamities and omens precisely to warn a ruler.

sentences.zh: 其變苟實，言之者何罪？

translations.literal: If the omen is real, what crime is there in speaking of it?
translations.idiomatic: If the portent is real, what crime lies in speaking of it?

sentences.zh: 其事必虛，聞之者足以自戒。

translations.literal: If the matter must be false, those who hear it have enough to guard themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If the report is false, those who hear it still have reason to take warning.

sentences.zh: 舜立謗木，良有以也。

translations.literal: Shun erected a wood for denunciations—there was good reason indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun set up a blame board for public grievances, and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 欲箝天下之口，其可得乎？

translations.literal: To clamp shut the mouths of all under Heaven—how can that be done?
translations.idiomatic: Can one truly silence every mouth in the empire?

sentences.zh: 此不足以加罪。”

translations.literal: This is not sufficient grounds for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That alone is not grounds for a charge.

sentences.zh: 特令赦之。

translations.literal: He specially ordered them pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them pardoned on the spot.

sentences.zh: 因謂處俊曰：“王者無外，何藉於守禦。

translations.literal: Then he said to Chujun: "A king has no outside; why rely on guards and defenses?
translations.idiomatic: He then told Chujun: "A true king knows no 'outside'; why lean on walls and guards?

sentences.zh: 雖然，重門擊柝，蓋備不虞，方知禁衛在於謹肅。

translations.literal: Even so, double gates and beating the watch-clapper prepare against the unforeseen—only then does one know that palace guards lie in strict discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, double gates and watchmen's clappers guard against surprise; one sees that palace security rests on strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 朕嚐以秦法猶為太寬，荊軻匹夫耳，而匕首竊發，始皇駭懼，莫有拒者，豈不由積習寬慢使其然乎？”

translations.literal: I once thought Qin law was still too lenient—Jing Ke was but a common man, yet his dagger was secretly drawn; the First Emperor was terrified and none resisted. Was this not because accumulated habits of laxity made it so?
translations.idiomatic: I once thought even Qin law was too lax—Jing Ke was a mere commoner, yet when he drew his hidden dagger the First Emperor was terrified and no one stopped him. Was that not the fruit of long slack habit?

sentences.zh: 處俊對曰：“此由法急所致，非寬慢也。”

translations.literal: Chujun replied: "This came from law being too harsh—not from laxity."
translations.idiomatic: Chujun answered: "That came from law being too harsh, not from laxity."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“何以知之？”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“秦法：輒升殿者，夷三族。

translations.literal: He replied: "Qin law: anyone who rashly ascended the hall—extinction of three kindreds."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Qin law punished anyone who entered the hall unbidden with extinction of three kindreds."

sentences.zh: 人皆懼族，安有敢拒者？

translations.literal: All feared extinction of kin—how could any dare resist?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared for their kin—who would dare resist?

sentences.zh: 逮乎魏武，法尚峻。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu of Wei, law still tended to severity.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wu of Wei, law was still severe.

sentences.zh: 臣見《魏令》云：‘京城有變，九卿各居其府。

translations.literal: I have seen the Wei Code: 'If the capital has an emergency, the Nine Ministers each remain in their offices.'
translations.idiomatic: I have read in the Wei Code: 'When the capital is disturbed, the Nine Ministers each stay in their own office.'

sentences.zh: ’其後嚴才作亂，與其徒屬數十人攻左掖門，魏武登銅雀台遠望，無敢救者。

translations.literal: Afterwards Yan Cai raised a disturbance; with several dozen followers he attacked the Left Flanking Gate. Emperor Wu ascended the Bronze Bird Terrace and looked from afar—none dared rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan Cai rebelled; with dozens of followers he attacked the Left Flanking Gate. Emperor Wu watched from the Bronze Bird Terrace—and no one dared move to help.

sentences.zh: 時王修為奉常，聞變召車馬，未至，便將官屬步至宮門。
