translations.literal: At the time Wang Xiu was Director of Ceremonial; hearing of the disturbance he summoned carriage and horse; before they arrived he led his staff on foot to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu was then Director of Ceremonial; hearing the alarm he called for a carriage, but before it came he marched his staff to the palace gate on foot.

sentences.zh: 魏武望見之，曰：‘彼來者必王修乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Wu saw him from afar and said: 'The one coming must be Wang Xiu!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu saw him and said: 'That must be Wang Xiu coming!'

sentences.zh: ’此由王修察變知機，違法赴難。

translations.literal: This was because Wang Xiu perceived the change and knew the moment, violating law to rush to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu read the crisis and broke the rule to answer the emergency.

sentences.zh: 向各守法，遂成其禍。

translations.literal: Had each kept to the law, the disaster would have been complete.
translations.idiomatic: Had each merely kept the letter of the law, disaster would have followed.

sentences.zh: 故王者設法敷化，不可以太急。

translations.literal: Therefore when a king sets law and spreads teaching, it cannot be too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's laws and teaching, then, must not be too harsh.

sentences.zh: 夫政寬則人慢，政急則人無所措手足。

translations.literal: When government is lenient people become lax; when government is harsh people have nowhere to put hands or feet.
translations.idiomatic: Lax rule breeds contempt; harsh rule leaves people at their wit's end.

sentences.zh: 聖王之道，寬猛相濟。

translations.literal: The way of sage kings balances leniency and severity.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king's way balances mercy and severity.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰‘不懈於位，人之攸塈’，謂仁政也；

translations.literal: The Odes say 'Unwearying in office, the people's resting-place'—this means benevolent government;
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Unwearying in office, the people's resting-place'—that is benevolent rule;

sentences.zh: 又曰‘式遏寇虐，無俾作慝’，謂威刑也。

translations.literal: And again 'Stop the robber and tyrant, do not let evil arise'—this means stern punishment.
translations.idiomatic: and again, 'Stop the robber and tyrant; do not let evil grow'—that is stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》曰‘高明柔克，沉潛剛克’，謂中道也。”

translations.literal: The Hong Fan says 'The exalted and bright overcome by gentleness; the deep and hidden overcome by firmness'—this means the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan says, 'What is bright is subdued by softness; what is hidden is subdued by firmness'—that is the middle way.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“善。”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 又有胡僧盧伽阿逸多受詔合長年藥，高宗將餌之。

translations.literal: There was also the foreign monk Luojia Ayiduo, who received an edict to compound a longevity elixir; Gaozong was about to take it.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk, Luojia Ayiduo, was ordered to brew a longevity potion, and Gaozong meant to take it.

sentences.zh: 處俊諫曰：“修短有命，未聞萬乘之主，輕服蕃夷之藥。

translations.literal: Chujun remonstrated: "Length of life has its decree; I have never heard of a lord of ten thousand chariots lightly taking barbarian medicine."
translations.idiomatic: Chujun remonstrated: "Life and death are fated. A sovereign should not lightly swallow barbarian drugs."

sentences.zh: 昔貞觀末年，先帝令婆羅門僧那羅邇娑寐依其本國舊方合長生藥。

translations.literal: Formerly at the end of Zhenguan, the late Emperor ordered the Brahmin monk Narayanasvamin to compound an immortality elixir according to his homeland's old formula.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenguan the late Emperor had the Brahmin Narayanasvamin brew an elixir of life by his homeland's recipe.

sentences.zh: 胡人有異術，征求靈草秘石，曆年而成。

translations.literal: The foreign monk had strange arts; seeking spiritual herbs and secret stones, it took years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: The foreigner's arts took years—rare herbs and secret stones gathered before the brew was done.

sentences.zh: 先帝服之，竟無異效，大漸之際，名醫莫知所為。

translations.literal: The late Emperor took it but in the end there was no special effect; at the final extremity even famous physicians knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor took it with no wondrous result; at the end even famous physicians could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 時議者歸罪於胡人，將申顯戮，又恐取笑夷狄，法遂不行。

translations.literal: At the time opinion blamed the foreign monk and execution was contemplated, but they feared ridicule from the barbarians, and the law was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion then blamed the foreigner and called for capital punishment, but fear of ridicule from the frontier peoples stayed the sentence.

sentences.zh: 龜鏡若是，惟陛下深察。”

translations.literal: A mirror like this—may Your Majesty examine deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the mirror before you; I beg Your Majesty to look hard at it.

sentences.zh: 高宗納之，但加盧伽為懷化大將軍，不服其藥。

translations.literal: Gaozong accepted this but only promoted Luojia to General Who Pacifies Transformation; he did not take the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong took his advice, made Luojia a General Who Pacifies Transformation, and did not take the drug.

sentences.zh: 尋而官名復舊。

translations.literal: Soon after the official titles reverted to the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the official titles returned to their former names.

sentences.zh: 處俊授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Chujun was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，加銀青光祿大夫，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the Silver Azure Light Steeds Grand Master title and transferred to Vice Director of the Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received Silver Azure Light Steeds Grand Master and became Vice Director of the Chancery.

sentences.zh: 四年，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he oversaw compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he supervised revision of the national history.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，高宗禦含元殿東翔鸞閣觀大酺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Gaozong attended the great communal feast from the Xianluan Pavilion east of the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan Gaozong watched the great feast from the Xianluan Pavilion east of Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 時京城四縣及太常音樂分為東西兩朋，帝令雍王賢為東朋，周王諱為西朋，務以角勝為樂。

translations.literal: At the time the four metropolitan counties and the Directorate of Music were divided into eastern and western teams; the Emperor made Prince Xian of Yong head the east and Prince of Zhou head the west, making competition their amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The four capital counties and the Directorate of Music were split into east and west teams; Prince Xian of Yong led the east and Prince of Zhou the west, vying for victory as sport.

sentences.zh: 處俊諫曰：：“臣聞禮所以示童子無誑者，恐其欺詐之心生也。

translations.literal: Chujun remonstrated: "I have heard that ritual teaches children not to deceive lest deceitful hearts arise."
translations.idiomatic: Chujun remonstrated: "Ritual teaches children not to lie, lest deceit take root."

sentences.zh: 伏以二王春秋尚少，意趣未定，當須推多讓美，相敬如一。

translations.literal: Humbly considering—the two princes are still young, their disposition not yet fixed; they should defer to one another and show mutual respect as one.
translations.idiomatic: Your two sons are still young and unsettled; they should defer to each other and treat one another with equal respect.

sentences.zh: 今忽分為二朋，遞相誇競。

translations.literal: Now suddenly divided into two teams, they boast and compete in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are split into rival teams and boast against one another.

sentences.zh: 且俳優小人，言辭無度，酣樂之後，難為禁止，恐其交爭勝負，譏誚失禮。

translations.literal: Moreover jesters and petty men speak without measure; after deep revelry they are hard to restrain—I fear they will quarrel over victory and defeat and jeer beyond propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Jesters and low characters speak without restraint; after heavy drinking they cannot be checked. They may quarrel over wins and losses and mock one another beyond all propriety.

sentences.zh: 非所以導仁義，示和睦也。”

translations.literal: This is not the way to lead in benevolence and righteousness or show harmony.
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to teach benevolence and righteousness or show harmony.

sentences.zh: 高宗矍然曰：“卿之遠識，非眾人所及也。”

translations.literal: Gaozong started and said: "Your far-sightedness—ordinary men cannot match it."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong started and said: "Your foresight is beyond what most men can reach."

sentences.zh: 遽令止之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 尋代閻立本為中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Yan Liben as Director of the Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Yan Liben as Director of the Chancery.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，兼太子賓客、檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he additionally served as Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he also served as Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，高宗以風疹欲遜位，令天後攝知國事，與宰相議之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Gaozong with wind rash wished to abdicate and have the Heavenly Empress govern state affairs; he discussed this with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Gaozong, afflicted with wind rash, wished to abdicate and let the Empress Wu govern; he discussed this with his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 處俊對曰：“嚐聞禮經云：‘天子理陽道，後理陰德。

translations.literal: Chujun replied: "I have heard the Ritual Canon say: 'The Son of Heaven governs the yang way; the Empress governs yin virtue.'"
translations.idiomatic: Chujun replied: "I have read in the Ritual Canon: 'The Son of Heaven administers the yang way; the Empress administers yin virtue.'"

sentences.zh: ’則帝之與後，猶日之與月，陽之與陰，各有所主守也。

translations.literal: Then Emperor and Empress are like sun and moon, yang and yin—each has what it governs and guards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and Empress are like sun and moon, yang and yin—each keeps its own domain.

sentences.zh: 陛下今欲違反此道，臣恐上則謫見於天，下則取怪於人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now wishes to violate this way—I fear above there will be reproof from Heaven, below ridicule from men.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty breaks this rule, I fear Heaven above will reprove you and men below will find it strange.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝著令，身崩後尚不許皇后臨朝，今陛下奈何遂欲躬自傳位於天後？

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Wei left an order that even after death the Empress was not permitted to attend court—how can Your Majesty now personally transfer rule to the Heavenly Empress?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei left orders that even after his death the Empress might not rule from court—how can Your Majesty now hand the realm to Empress Wu?

sentences.zh: 況天下者，高祖、太宗二聖之天下，非陛下之天下也。

translations.literal: Moreover the realm is the realm of the two sages Gaozu and Taizong—not Your Majesty's private realm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the realm belongs to the two sages Gaozu and Taizong—not to Your Majesty alone to give away.

sentences.zh: 陛下正合謹守宗廟，傳之子孫，誠不可持國與人，有私於後族。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should strictly guard the ancestral temples and pass rule to sons and grandsons—it truly cannot be given to another out of favor to the maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should guard the ancestral temples and pass the realm to your sons and grandsons—not give the state away for the sake of the Empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 伏乞特垂詳納。”

translations.literal: Humbly I beg Your Majesty especially to consider and accept this.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully and accept it.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李義琰進曰：“處俊所引經旨，足可依憑，惟聖慮無疑，則蒼生幸甚。”

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancery Li Yiyan advanced and said: "The canonical texts Chujun cites are fully reliable—if Your Majesty's sage mind is without doubt, the common people will be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Yiyan said: "Chujun's scriptural citations can be relied on; if Your Majesty's mind is firm, the people will be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“是。”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And so the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，加金紫光祿大夫，行太子左庶子，並依舊知政事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng he was given Gold and Purple Light Steeds Grand Master, Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, continuing in governance as before, overseeing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng he received Gold and Purple Light Steeds Grand Master, served as Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, continued in governance, and oversaw the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，代張文瓘為侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he replaced Zhang Wenguan as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he replaced Zhang Wenguan as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 處俊性儉素，土木形骸，自參綜朝政，每與上言議，必引經籍以應對，多有匡益，甚得大臣之體。

translations.literal: Chujun was by nature frugal and plain, with the form of earth and wood; from the time he joined governance, whenever he debated with the Emperor he always cited the classics in reply—much corrective benefit, very much in the manner of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and plain, almost austere in person, once he entered government he always answered the Emperor with citations from the classics; his counsel often helped, and he truly bore himself as a chief minister should.

sentences.zh: 侍中、平恩公許圉師，即處俊之舅，早同州裏，俱宦達於時。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Duke of Ping'en Xu Tushi was Chujun's maternal uncle; they had early been from the same prefecture and both risen to office in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xu Tushi, Duke of Ping'en, was his maternal uncle; they were from the same district and both rose high in office.

sentences.zh: 又其鄉人田氏、彭氏，以殖貨見稱。

translations.literal: Also fellow townsfolk the Tian and Peng clans were famed for amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsmen, the Tian and Peng families, were known for amassing wealth.

sentences.zh: 有彭誌筠，顯慶中，上表請以家絹布二萬段助軍，詔受其絹萬匹，特授奉議郎，仍布告天下。

translations.literal: There was Peng Zhijun who in Xianqing memorialized offering twenty thousand bolts of home silk and cloth to aid the army; an edict accepted ten thousand bolts of silk and specially appointed him Gentleman for Advising, and it was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zhijun, in Xianqing, offered twenty thousand bolts of silk and cloth from his household to aid the army; the court accepted ten thousand bolts, made him a Gentleman for Advising, and proclaimed it empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 故江、淮間語曰：“貴如許、郝，富若田、彭。”

translations.literal: Hence a saying between the Yangzi and Huai: "Noble as Xu and Hao, rich as Tian and Peng."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying in the Jianghuai region: "Noble as the Xu and Hao; rich as the Tian and Peng."

sentences.zh: 處俊遷太子少保。

translations.literal: Chujun was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開耀元年薨，年七十五，贈開府儀同三司、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyao he died at age seventy-five; posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Opening with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and Great Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Kaiyao at seventy-five; posthumously he received Grand Master of Splendid Opening with Three Excellencies ceremonial and Great Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗甚傷悼之，顧謂侍臣曰：“處俊誌存忠正，兼有學識。

translations.literal: Gaozong grieved deeply and turning to the attendant ministers said: "Chujun's will held loyalty and rectitude, and he also had learning."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong grieved deeply and told his attendants: "Chujun was loyal and upright in heart and well learned besides."

sentences.zh: 至於雕飾服玩，雖極知無益，然常人不能抑情棄舍，皆好尚奢侈，處俊嚐保其質素，終始不渝。

translations.literal: As for ornamental attire and playthings—though he knew extremely well they were useless, yet ordinary people cannot restrain desire and discard them; all prefer luxury; Chujun always kept his plain quality from beginning to end without change.
translations.idiomatic: Ornaments and fine trappings—though he knew they were useless, most men cannot give them up and love luxury; Chujun always kept to plain living, unchanged to the end.

sentences.zh: 雖非元勳佐命，固亦多時驅使。

translations.literal: Though not a founding minister who aided the mandate, he nevertheless served for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He was no founding minister who shaped the dynasty, yet he served faithfully for many years.

sentences.zh: 又見遺表，憂國忘家，今既雲亡，深可傷惜。”

translations.literal: Also seeing his final memorial, he forgot family in concern for the state—now that he is gone, deeply to be mourned.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial showed concern for the state above his own household; now that he is gone, the loss is grievous.

sentences.zh: 即於光順門舉哀一日，不視事，終祭以少牢，贈絹布八百段、米粟八百碩。

translations.literal: Immediately at the Gate of Glorious Compliance mourning was observed for one day; he did not attend to affairs; final sacrifice with the lesser offering; gift of eight hundred bolts of silk and cloth and eight hundred measures of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned at the Gate of Glorious Compliance for a day and held no audience; the final rites used the lesser offering; he granted eight hundred bolts of silk and cloth and eight hundred measures of grain.

sentences.zh: 令百官赴哭，給靈輿，並家口遞還鄉，官供葬事。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to attend the lamentation, provided the funeral bier, and sent household members back to their home district by relay post; the state supplied the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to attend the mourning, supplied the funeral bier, sent the household home by official relay, and paid for the burial.

sentences.zh: 其子秘書郎北叟上表辭所贈賜及葬遞之事，高宗不許。

translations.literal: His son Beishou, Secretariat Gentleman, memorialized declining the gifts and burial relay; Gaozong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Beishou, a Secretariat Gentleman, petitioned to refuse the gifts and relay transport; Gaozong refused.

sentences.zh: 侍中裴炎曰：“處俊臨亡，臣往見之，屬臣曰：‘生既無益明時，死後何宜煩費。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Pei Yan said: "When Chujun was dying I went to see him; he entrusted me, saying: 'Living I already benefited the enlightened age little—after death why should there be troublesome expense?'
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Pei Yan said: "At Chujun's deathbed I visited him; he told me: 'Living, I did little for the realm—after death why burden the state with expense?'

sentences.zh: 瞑目之後，儻有恩賜贈物，及歸鄉遞送，葬日營造，不欲勞官司供給。

translations.literal: After eyes close, if there are gracious gifts or relay transport home, or construction on the burial day—I do not wish to trouble official offices for supply."
translations.idiomatic: After I close my eyes, should there be imperial gifts, relay escort home, or work on burial day, I do not wish officials burdened on my account.'

sentences.zh: ’”高宗深嘉歎之，從其遺意，唯加贈物而已。

translations.literal: Gaozong greatly praised and sighed; following his dying wish he only added gift items.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong admired this deeply, followed his last wish, and added only the gifts.

sentences.zh: 處俊孫象賢，垂拱中為太子通事舍人，坐事伏誅，臨刑言多不順。

translations.literal: Chujun's grandson Xiang Xian, in the Chuigong era served as Palace Attendant for Communications to the Heir Apparent; condemned for an offense and executed, at execution his words were largely insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xiang Xian, a Palace Attendant for Communications to the Heir Apparent under Chuigong, was executed for an offense; at the block his words were defiant.

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，令斬訖，仍支解其體，發其父母墳墓，焚爇屍體，處俊亦坐斫棺毀柩。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly enraged; ordered him beheaded when done, then dismembered the body, opened his parents' graves, burned the corpses; Chujun too was implicated—his coffin hacked and bier destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu flew into a rage, had him beheaded and dismembered, opened his parents' graves and burned their corpses; Chujun too was implicated—his coffin was hacked open and bier destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自此法司每將殺人，必先以木丸塞其口，然後加刑，訖於則天之代。

translations.literal: From this time onward, whenever the legal authorities were about to put someone to death, they would first stop up the mouth with a wooden pellet and only then apply punishment—a practice that lasted through the age of Empress Wu Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the courts were about to execute a prisoner, they first stuffed a wooden gag into the mouth and only then applied the sentence. The custom endured through Wu Zetian's reign.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian came from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖伯鳳，周驃騎大將軍、汾州刺史、琅邪郡公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bo Feng was Cavalry General-in-Chief under Zhou, governor of Fen Prefecture, and Duke of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bo Feng had served Zhou as Cavalry General-in-Chief, governor of Fenzhou, and Duke of Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖定高，馮翊郡守，襲封琅邪公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ding Gao was prefect of Fengyi Commandery and inherited the title Duke of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ding Gao was prefect of Fengyi and inherited the dukedom of Langye.

sentences.zh: 父仁基，隋左光祿大夫，陷於王世充，後謀歸國，事泄遇害；

translations.literal: His father Renji was Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness under the Sui. He fell into Wang Shichong's hands; later he plotted to return to the Tang, but when the plot was exposed he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renji had been Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness under the Sui. Trapped in Wang Shichong's domain, he later plotted to rejoin the Tang court; the plot was discovered and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 武德中，贈原州都督，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he was posthumously made Military Governor of Yuan Prefecture, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude period he was posthumously appointed military governor of Yuanzhou and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 行儉幼以門蔭補弘文生。

translations.literal: Xingjian in youth entered the Hongwen Academy by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xingjian entered the Hongwen Academy through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，舉明經，拜左屯衛倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Warehouse Clerk of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed warehouse clerk in the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 時蘇定方為大將軍，甚奇之，盡以用兵奇術授行儉。

translations.literal: At the time Su Dingfang was a great general. He took a special liking to Xingjian and taught him all his extraordinary arts of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang was then a great general. He took a keen interest in Xingjian and taught him every secret of his art of war.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，六遷長安令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, after six promotions he became magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing, after six promotions, he became magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時高宗將廢皇后王氏而立武昭儀，行儉以為國家憂患必從此始，與太尉長孫無忌、尚書左僕射褚遂良私議其事，大理袁公瑜於昭儀母榮國夫人譖之，由是左授西州都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and install Consort Wu as empress. Xingjian believed that calamity for the state would begin from this, and privately discussed the matter with Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Chu Suiliang. Yuan Gongyu of the Court of Judicial Review denounced them to Consort Wu's mother, the Lady of Rong State, and for this Xingjian was demoted to chief secretary of the Western Prefecture Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was preparing to depose Empress Wang and elevate Consort Wu, Xingjian judged that national disaster would begin there. He spoke of it in private with Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and Left Vice Director Chu Suiliang. Yuan Gongyu of the Court of Judicial Review informed Consort Wu's mother, the Lady of Rong State, and Xingjian was demoted to chief secretary of the Western Prefecture Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年，累拜安西大都護，西域諸國多慕義歸降，征拜司文少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde, after repeated promotions he was appointed Grand Protector General of Anxi. Many states of the Western Regions admired his virtue and submitted; he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Literary Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Linde he rose to Grand Protector General of Anxi. Many western kingdoms submitted in admiration of his authority, and he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of the Court of Literary Scholars.

sentences.zh: 總章中，遷司列少常伯。

translations.literal: During the Zongzhang era he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: During Zongzhang he was moved to Vice Director of the Court of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，官名復舊，改為吏部侍郎，與李敬玄為貳，同時典選十餘年，甚有能名，時人稱為裴、李。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng, when official titles were restored to their old forms, he was made Vice Minister of Personnel and served as second to Li Jingxuan. For more than ten years they jointly managed selection together, with great reputation for ability, and people of the time called them Pei and Li.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianheng, when the old titles were restored, he became Vice Minister of Personnel and served alongside Li Jingxuan as his deputy. For more than ten years the two men jointly ran selection, earning a great name for competence; contemporaries spoke of them as Pei and Li.

sentences.zh: 行儉始設長名姓曆榜，引銓注等法，又定州縣升降、官資高下，以為故事。

translations.literal: Xingjian first established the long-register roster, citation and appointment regulations, and other methods, and also fixed the rise and fall of prefectures and counties and the grades of office and salary, which thereafter became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian first instituted the long-register roster, citation and appointment rules, and related methods, and also fixed the ranking of prefectures and counties and the grades of office and emolument—practices that thereafter became precedent.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he was given the additional title Silver Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan he received the additional rank of Silver Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 高宗以行儉工於草書。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong considered Xingjian skilled in cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong admired Xingjian's skill in cursive script.

sentences.zh: 嚐以絹素百卷，令行儉草書《文選》一部，帝覽之稱善，賜帛五百段。

translations.literal: Once he gave Xingjian a hundred rolls of silk and ordered him to write out the Wen Xuan in cursive. The emperor read it and praised it, bestowing five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he gave Xingjian a hundred rolls of silk and had him write out the Wen Xuan in cursive. The emperor read the work, praised it, and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 行儉嚐謂人曰：“褚遂良非精筆佳墨，未嚐輒書，不擇筆墨而妍捷者，唯餘及虞世南耳。”

translations.literal: Xingjian once said to others, "Chu Suiliang will not write unless the brush and ink are fine; among those who write beautifully and swiftly without choosing brush or ink, only I and Yu Shinan remain."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian once remarked, "Chu Suiliang will not write unless the brush and ink are perfect. Of those who can write beautifully and swiftly without caring what tools they use, only Yu Shinan and I remain."

sentences.zh: 三年，吐蕃背叛，詔行儉為洮州道左二軍總管。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Tibet rebelled, an edict appointed Xingjian Left Second Army Commander of the Taozhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Tibet rebelled, an edict made Xingjian Left Second Army Commander on the Taozhou route.

sentences.zh: 尋又為泰州鎮撫右軍總管，並受元帥周王節度。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was also made Right Army Commander of the Taizhou Pacification Command, both posts subject to the command of the Prince of Zhou as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also appointed Right Army Commander of the Taizhou pacification force, both commands falling under the Prince of Zhou as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，十姓可汗阿史那匐延都支及李遮匐扇動蕃落，侵逼安西，連和吐蕃，議者欲發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Ashina Fuyan Duzhi, khaghan of the Ten Tribes, and Li Zhefu stirred up the tribal peoples, pressed upon Anxi, and joined forces with Tibet. Those who deliberated wished to send troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng, Ashina Fuyan Duzhi, khaghan of the Ten Tribes, and Li Zhefu stirred up the frontier tribes, threatened Anxi, and allied with Tibet. The court debated sending an army against them.

sentences.zh: 行儉建議曰：“吐蕃叛渙，干戈未息，敬玄、審禮，失律喪元，安可更為西方生事？

translations.literal: Xingjian submitted a proposal, saying, "Tibet has rebelled and scattered; the weapons of war have not yet ceased. Jingxuan and Shenli lost their discipline and their lives—how can we create fresh trouble in the west?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian proposed: "Tibet is in revolt and unrest continues. Jingxuan and Shenli broke discipline and lost their lives—why should we stir up new trouble in the west?"

sentences.zh: 今波斯王身沒，其子泥涅師師充質在京，望差使往波斯冊立，即路由二蕃部落，便宜從事，必可有功。”

translations.literal: Now the king of Persia has died, and his son Nipour, who serves as hostage in the capital, hopes that an envoy may be sent to invest him in Persia. The route passes through the territories of the two rebel peoples; if we act as circumstances allow, success is certain.
translations.idiomatic: The Persian king is dead, and his son Nipour, held as hostage in the capital, asks that an envoy be sent to invest him. The road runs through the lands of both rebel peoples; if we seize the opportunity as we go, we can surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 高宗從之，因命行儉冊送波斯王，仍為安撫大食使。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong agreed and therefore ordered Xingjian to escort and invest the king of Persia, while also making him envoy to pacify the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong accepted the plan and ordered Xingjian to escort and invest the Persian king, appointing him at the same time envoy to pacify the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 途經莫賀延磧，屬風沙晦暝，導者益迷。

translations.literal: Passing through the Mohe-Yan Desert, they encountered wind and sand and dim darkness, and the guides became ever more lost.
translations.idiomatic: On the road through the Mohe-Yan Desert, wind and sand blotted out the sky and the guides lost their way.

sentences.zh: 行儉命下營，虔誠致祭，令告將吏，泉井非遙。

translations.literal: Xingjian ordered the camp struck, performed a sincere sacrifice, and announced to officers and men that springs and wells were not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian ordered camp struck, offered a solemn sacrifice, and told officers and men that water was not far off.

sentences.zh: 俄而雲收風靜，行數百步，水草甚豐，後來之人，莫知其處。

translations.literal: Before long the clouds cleared and the wind stilled. After marching several hundred paces they found abundant grass and water. Later travelers never knew where the place was.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the clouds lifted and the wind fell. After a few hundred paces they came upon rich grass and water. Later travelers could never find the spot again.

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅服，比之貳師將軍。

translations.literal: All were pleased and submitted, comparing him to the General of the Ershi.
translations.idiomatic: The men were won over entirely, and likened him to General Li of the Ershi.

sentences.zh: 至西州，人吏郊迎，行儉召其豪傑子弟千餘人隨己而西。

translations.literal: When he reached Xizhou, officials and clerks came out to the suburbs to welcome him. Xingjian summoned more than a thousand sons of the local magnates to accompany him westward.
translations.idiomatic: At Xizhou, officials and clerks met him outside the walls. Xingjian called up more than a thousand sons of the local magnates to march west with him.

sentences.zh: 乃揚言紿其下曰：“今正炎蒸，熱阪難冒，涼秋之後，方可漸行。”

translations.literal: He then spread a false report among his subordinates, saying, "It is now the height of heat; the hot passes are hard to brave. Only after the cool of autumn can we gradually set out."
translations.idiomatic: He then deceived his subordinates with a public announcement: "The heat is at its worst and the hot passes are impossible to cross. We can move only after the cool of autumn."

sentences.zh: 都支覘知之，遂不設備。

translations.literal: Duzhi learned of this through spies and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi learned of this through spies and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 行儉仍召四鎮諸蕃酋長豪傑謂曰：“憶昔此遊，未嚐厭倦，雖還京輦，無時暫忘。

translations.literal: Xingjian then summoned the chieftains and magnates of the four garrisons and the various tribes, saying, "I remember this country from former travels and never grew weary of it. Though I returned to the capital, I never forgot it for a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian then summoned the chieftains and magnates of the four garrisons and the frontier tribes and said, "I remember these lands from my earlier service and never tired of them. Though I returned to the capital, I never forgot them for a moment."

sentences.zh: 今因是行，欲尋舊賞，誰能從吾獵也？”

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of this journey, I wish to revisit old pleasures. Who will hunt with me?
translations.idiomatic: On this journey I mean to revisit old pleasures. Who will hunt with me?"

sentences.zh: 是時蕃酋子弟投募者僅萬人。

translations.literal: At that time nearly ten thousand sons of tribal chieftains volunteered.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand sons of tribal chieftains volunteered.

sentences.zh: 行儉假為畋遊，教試部伍，數日，遂倍道而進。

translations.literal: Xingjian pretended to go hunting and had them drill in formation. After several days he doubled his pace and pressed forward.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian feigned a hunting expedition and drilled them in formation. After several days he doubled his pace and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 去都支部落十餘里，先遣都支所親問其安否，外示閑暇，似非討襲，續又使人趣召相見。

translations.literal: When he was a little more than ten li from Duzhi's tribe, he first sent one of Duzhi's intimates to inquire after his health, outwardly showing leisure as though he were not on a punitive raid; then he sent another man to summon him to a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than ten li from Duzhi's camp, he first sent one of Duzhi's intimates to inquire after his health, outwardly at ease as though no attack were planned; then he sent another messenger to summon him to a meeting.

sentences.zh: 都支先與遮匐通謀，秋中擬拒漢使，卒聞軍到，計無所出，自率兒侄首領等五百餘騎就營來謁，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Duzhi had earlier conspired with Zhefu and in mid-autumn planned to resist the Han envoy. When he suddenly heard that the army had arrived and could devise no plan, he himself led more than five hundred mounted followers—sons, nephews, and chieftains—to the camp to pay respects, and was there seized.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi had already conspired with Zhefu and planned to resist the imperial envoy by mid-autumn. When the army appeared without warning and he could think of no countermove, he led more than five hundred mounted followers—sons, nephews, and chieftains—to the camp to pay respects, and was seized on the spot.

sentences.zh: 是日，傳其契箭，諸部酋長悉來請命，並執送碎葉城。

translations.literal: That same day, by transmitting his command arrows, all the tribal chieftains came to submit and were escorted to Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, by passing on his command arrows, he brought every tribal chieftain to submit; all were sent under guard to Suyab.

sentences.zh: 簡其精騎，輕齎曉夜前進，將虜遮匐。

translations.literal: He selected elite horsemen, traveled light, and pressed forward day and night to capture Zhefu.
translations.idiomatic: He picked out elite horsemen, traveled light, and pressed forward day and night to take Zhefu.

sentences.zh: 途中果獲都支還使，與遮匐使同來。

translations.literal: On the road he indeed captured Duzhi's returning envoy, who was coming together with Zhefu's messenger.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he captured Duzhi's returning envoy, traveling together with Zhefu's messenger.

sentences.zh: 行儉釋遮匐行人，令先往曉喻其主，兼述都支已擒，遮匐尋復來降。

translations.literal: Xingjian released Zhefu's messenger and had him go ahead to instruct his master, while also stating that Duzhi had already been taken. Zhefu soon submitted in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian released Zhefu's messenger and sent him ahead to warn his master and report that Duzhi had already been captured. Zhefu soon surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 於是將吏已下立碑於碎葉城以紀其功，擒都支、遮匐而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and men from the ranks downward erected a stele at Suyab to record the achievement, and returned after capturing Duzhi and Zhefu.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men then raised a stele at Suyab to record the victory, and returned with Duzhi and Zhefu as captives.

sentences.zh: 高宗廷勞之曰：“比以西服未寧，遣卿總兵討逐，孤軍深入，經途萬里。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong received him at court and praised him, saying, "Because the western lands were not yet settled, I sent you to command troops in pursuit. You advanced alone deep into enemy country, traveling ten thousand li on the road."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong received him at court and praised him: "Because the western lands were still unsettled, I sent you to command troops in pursuit. You advanced deep into enemy country with a lone force, traveling ten thousand li on the road."

sentences.zh: 卿權略有聞，誠節夙著，兵不血刃，而凶黨殄滅。

translations.literal: Your resourcefulness in stratagem is well known, and your loyalty and integrity long established. Without bloodshed you destroyed the wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: Your resourcefulness is well known, and your loyalty long established. Without drawing blood you destroyed the rebel faction.

sentences.zh: 伐叛柔服，深副朕委。”

translations.literal: To punish rebels and soothe those who submit fully matches what I entrusted to you.
translations.idiomatic: To punish rebels and win over those who submit—this fully fulfills what I entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 尋又賜宴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also granted a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: He soon granted a banquet as well.

sentences.zh: 謂行儉曰：“卿文武兼資，今故授卿二職。”

translations.literal: He said to Xingjian, "You combine civil and military talent. I therefore now grant you two offices."
translations.idiomatic: He told Xingjian, "You combine civil and military talent. I therefore grant you two offices at once."

sentences.zh: 即日拜禮部尚書，兼檢校右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: That same day Xingjian was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Inspector General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xingjian was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Inspector General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 調露元年，突厥阿史德溫傅反，單於管內二十四州並叛應之，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiaolu, Ashide Wenfu of the Turks rebelled. Twenty-four prefectures within the Protectorate of the Khaghan all rebelled in response, numbering several hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiaolu, the Turk Ashide Wenfu rebelled. Twenty-four prefectures within the Protectorate of the Khaghan rose with him, fielding several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 單於都護蕭嗣業率兵討之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Protector-General of the Khaghan Xiao Siye led troops to punish them and was in turn defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Xiao Siye marched against them and was defeated in turn.

sentences.zh: 於是以行儉為定襄道行軍大總管，率太仆少卿李思文、營州都督周道務等部兵十八萬，並西軍程務挺、東軍李文柬等總三十餘萬，連亙數千里，並受行儉節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xingjian was made Great General on Campaign of the Dingxiang Circuit. He led Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Siwen, Military Governor of Ying Prefecture Zhou Daowu, and others with a force of one hundred eighty thousand, together with Cheng Wuting of the Western Army and Li Wenjian of the Eastern Army and others totaling more than three hundred thousand, stretching in unbroken lines for several thousand li, all subject to Xingjian's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was then made Great General on Campaign of the Dingxiang route. He led Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Siwen, Military Governor of Yingzhou Zhou Daowu, and others with one hundred eighty thousand men, while Cheng Wuting of the western force and Li Wenjian of the eastern force brought the total to more than three hundred thousand. The columns stretched unbroken for thousands of li, all under Xingjian's command.

sentences.zh: 唐世出師之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: Never in the Tang had an expedition been so grand.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang had never mounted so great an expedition.

sentences.zh: 行儉行至朔州，知蕭嗣業以運糧被掠，兵多餒死，遂詐為糧車三百乘，每車伏壯士五人，各齎陌刀、勁弩，以羸兵數百人援車，兼伏精兵，令居險以待之。

translations.literal: When Xingjian reached Shuozhou and learned that Xiao Siye's grain convoys had been plundered and many soldiers had starved to death, he feigned three hundred grain wagons. In each wagon five stalwart men lay concealed, each carrying a modao and a powerful crossbow. Several hundred weak soldiers escorted the wagons, while elite troops were also hidden and ordered to wait in difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingjian reached Shuozhou and learned that Xiao Siye's grain convoys had been raided and many soldiers had starved, he set out three hundred decoy grain wagons. Five stalwart men lay hidden in each wagon, armed with modao and powerful crossbows. A few hundred weak soldiers escorted the train while elite troops waited in ambush on difficult ground.

sentences.zh: 賊果大下，羸兵棄車散走。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came down in force. The weak soldiers abandoned the wagons and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came down in force. The weak escort abandoned the wagons and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊驅車就泉水。

translations.literal: The bandits drove the wagons toward a spring.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove the wagons toward a spring.

sentences.zh: 解鞍牧馬，方擬取糧，車中壯士齊發，伏兵亦至，殺獲殆盡，餘眾奔潰。

translations.literal: They unslung saddles and grazed horses, and were just about to take the grain when the stalwarts in the wagons struck together and the ambush also arrived. Nearly all were killed or captured; the remainder fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: They unslung saddles to graze their horses and were about to seize the grain when the men in the wagons struck together and the ambush closed in. Nearly all were killed or captured; the rest broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 自是續遣糧車，無敢近之者。

translations.literal: Thereafter grain wagons sent afterward were never again approached.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one dared approach the grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 及軍至單於之北，際晚下營，壕塹方周，遽令移就崇岡。

translations.literal: When the army reached the north of the Protectorate of the Khaghan, it made camp at dusk. The trenches had just been completed when he suddenly ordered the camp moved to a high ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the country north of the Protectorate of the Khaghan, it encamped at dusk. The trenches had barely been finished when Xingjian suddenly ordered the camp moved to a high ridge.

sentences.zh: 將士皆以士眾方就安堵，不可勞擾，行儉不從，更令促之。

translations.literal: Officers and men all said that the troops had just settled into comfort and ought not be troubled, but Xingjian would not listen and ordered them to hurry all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men protested that the troops had just settled and should not be disturbed, but Xingjian refused and ordered the move accelerated.

sentences.zh: 比夜，風雨暴至，前設營所水深丈餘，將士莫不歎伏。

translations.literal: By night a violent storm suddenly came. The water at the former camp site was more than ten feet deep, and officers and men all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: That night a violent storm burst upon them. The former camp site stood more than ten feet deep in water, and officers and men marveled.

sentences.zh: 賊眾於黑山拒戰，行儉頻戰皆捷，前後殺虜不可勝數。

translations.literal: The rebel host resisted at Black Mountain. Xingjian fought repeatedly and was victorious each time, killing and capturing beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels made their stand at Black Mountain. Xingjian fought again and again and won every engagement, killing and capturing beyond count.

sentences.zh: 偽可汗泥熟匐為其下所殺，以其首來降，又擒其大首領奉職而還。

translations.literal: The false khaghan Nishou Fu was killed by his subordinates, who brought his head to surrender. Xingjian also captured the great chieftain Fengzhi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender khaghan Nishou Fu was killed by his own followers, who brought his head in surrender. Xingjian also captured the great chieftain Fengzhi and returned.

sentences.zh: 餘黨走依狼山。

translations.literal: The remaining band fled and relied upon Lang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels fled to Lang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 行儉既回，阿史那伏念又偽稱可汗，與溫傅合勢，鳩集餘眾。

translations.literal: After Xingjian had returned, Ashina Funian again falsely styled himself khaghan, joined forces with Wenfu, and gathered the remnant host.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingjian returned, Ashina Funian again proclaimed himself khaghan, joined Wenfu, and rallied the remnant forces.

sentences.zh: 明年，行儉復總諸軍討之。

translations.literal: The next year Xingjian again commanded the armies to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xingjian again took command of the armies to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 頓軍於代州之陘口，縱反間說伏念與溫傅，令相猜貳。

translations.literal: He halted the army at the Pass of Daizhou and spread counter-intelligence to sow suspicion between Funian and Wenfu.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at the Pass of Daizhou and spread counter-intelligence to set Funian and Wenfu against each other.

sentences.zh: 伏念恐懼，密送降款，仍請自效。

translations.literal: Funian was afraid and secretly sent terms of surrender, asking moreover to prove his loyalty by action.
translations.idiomatic: Funian, in fear, secretly sent terms of surrender and offered to prove his loyalty in deed.

sentences.zh: 行儉不泄其事，而密表以聞。

translations.literal: Xingjian did not reveal the matter but secretly memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian kept the matter secret and memorialized the throne privately.

sentences.zh: 數日，有煙塵漲天而至，斥候惶惑來白，行儉召三軍謂曰：“此是伏念執溫傅來降，非他。

translations.literal: After several days dust and smoke filled the sky as they approached. Scouts came in alarm to report, but Xingjian summoned the three armies and said, "This is Funian bringing Wenfu in surrender—nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later a cloud of dust filled the sky as a column approached. Alarmed scouts reported, but Xingjian assembled the three armies and said, "This is Funian bringing Wenfu in surrender—nothing else."

sentences.zh: 然受降如受敵，但須嚴備。”

translations.literal: Yet receiving surrender is like receiving the enemy; we need only make strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Still, to receive a surrender is like facing an enemy—we must remain on strict guard."

sentences.zh: 更遣單使迎前勞之。

translations.literal: He again sent a single envoy forward to welcome and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a lone envoy forward to welcome and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 少間，伏念果率其屬縛溫傅詣軍門請罪，盡平突厥餘黨。

translations.literal: Before long Funian indeed led his followers, bound Wenfu, and came to the camp gate to ask punishment, and the remaining Turk faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Funian indeed arrived with his followers, Wenfu bound, and asked punishment at the camp gate. The remaining Turk forces were completely pacified.

sentences.zh: 高宗大悅，遣戶部尚書崔知悌赴軍勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was greatly pleased and sent Minister of Revenue Cui Zhiti to the army to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was greatly pleased and sent Minister of Revenue Cui Zhiti to the army to offer praise.

sentences.zh: 侍中裴炎害行儉之功，總管程務挺、張虔勖上言：“伏念為子營逼逐，又磧北回紇等同向南逼之，窘急而降。”

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Yan, jealous of Xingjian's achievement, and the commanders Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu submitted a memorial, saying, "Funian was driven to surrender because his son was pressed hard and because the Uyghurs north of the desert and others likewise pressed him from the south. He submitted in desperation."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Yan, envious of Xingjian's achievement, and the commanders Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu memorialized: "Funian surrendered only because his son was hard pressed and because the Uyghurs north of the desert and others pressed him from the south. He submitted in desperation."

sentences.zh: 由是行儉之功不錄，斬伏念及溫傅於都市。

translations.literal: For this Xingjian's achievement was not recorded, and Funian and Wenfu were beheaded in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: On this account Xingjian's victory went unrecorded, and Funian and Wenfu were beheaded in the capital market.

sentences.zh: 行儉歎曰：“渾、浚前事，古今恥之。

translations.literal: Xingjian sighed and said, "The precedents of Hun and Jun—such things have shamed all ages."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian sighed and said, "What Hun and Jun did—such deeds have shamed every age."

sentences.zh: 但恐殺降之後，無復來者。”

translations.literal: I only fear that after killing those who surrender, none will come again.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once surrendered men are killed, none will ever come again."

sentences.zh: 因稱疾不出，以勳封聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: He therefore pleaded illness and did not go out, and for his merit was enfeoffed Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and withdrew from public life. For his merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，十姓偽可汗車薄反叛，詔復以行儉為金牙道大總管，率十將軍以討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Che Bo, false khaghan of the Ten Tribes, rebelled. An edict again made Xingjian Great General of the Jinya Circuit and ordered him to lead ten generals to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchun, Che Bo, pretender khaghan of the Ten Tribes, rebelled. An edict again made Xingjian Great General of the Jinya route and ordered him to lead ten generals against him.

sentences.zh: 師未行。

translations.literal: The army had not yet marched.
translations.idiomatic: The army had not yet set out.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，行儉病卒，年六十四，贈幽州都督，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year Xingjian died of illness at the age of sixty-four. He was posthumously made Military Governor of You Prefecture, with the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year Xingjian died of illness at sixty-four. He was posthumously appointed military governor of Youzhou and given the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 特詔令皇太子差六品京官一人檢校家事，五六年間，待兒孫稍成長日停。

translations.literal: A special edict ordered the Crown Prince to assign a capital official of the sixth rank to oversee the household affairs, to continue for five or six years until the grandchildren had grown somewhat, and then cease.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict ordered the Crown Prince to assign a sixth-rank capital official to oversee the household, continuing for five or six years until the grandchildren had grown, and then to stop.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，追贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Xingjian was further posthumously made Grand Military Governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Xingjian was further posthumously made Grand Military Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，撰《草字雜體》數萬言，並傳於代。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan and composed Miscellaneous Forms of Cursive Characters in tens of thousands of words; both were handed down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan and a Miscellaneous Forms of Cursive Characters of tens of thousands of words; both circulated in later ages.

sentences.zh: 又撰《選譜》十卷，安置軍營、行陣部統、克料勝負、甄別器能等四十六訣，則天令秘書監武承嗣詣宅，並密收入內。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Register of Selection in ten juan, and forty-six maxims on deploying camps, organizing battle formations and units, calculating victory and defeat, and distinguishing talent and capacity. Empress Wu ordered Palace Library Director Wu Chengsi to go to his residence, and all were secretly taken into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Register of Selection in ten juan and forty-six maxims on camp deployment, battle formation and unit organization, calculating victory and defeat, and judging talent and capacity. Empress Wu ordered Palace Library Director Wu Chengsi to his residence, and all were secretly taken into the palace archives.

sentences.zh: 行儉尤曉陰陽、算術，兼有人倫之鑒。

translations.literal: Xingjian was especially versed in yin-yang lore and calculation, and also possessed insight into human character.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was especially skilled in yin-yang lore and calculation, and possessed a keen eye for human character.

sentences.zh: 自掌選及為大總管，凡遇賢俊，無不甄采，每製敵摧凶，必先期捷日。

translations.literal: From the time he managed selection until he served as great general, whenever he encountered worthy talent he never failed to discover and promote them. Whenever he prepared to strike an enemy and destroy a foe, he always first fixed in advance the day of victory.
translations.idiomatic: From his years managing selection through his service as great general, whenever he met worthy talent he discovered and promoted them. Whenever he prepared to meet an enemy and destroy a foe, he always fixed the day of victory in advance.

sentences.zh: 時有後進楊炯、王勃、盧照鄰、駱賓王並以文章見稱，吏部侍郎李敬玄盛為延譽，引以示行儉，行儉曰：“才名有之，爵祿蓋寡。

translations.literal: At the time the younger talents Yang Jiong, Wang Bo, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were all famed for their writing. Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jingxuan greatly praised them and introduced them to Xingjian. Xingjian said, "They have talent and name, but rank and emolument will be meager."
translations.idiomatic: The rising writers Yang Jiong, Wang Bo, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were then celebrated for their prose. Vice Minister Li Jingxuan praised them lavishly and presented them to Xingjian. Xingjian said, "They have talent and fame, but rank and salary will be thin."

sentences.zh: 楊應至令長，餘並鮮能令終。”

translations.literal: Yang will reach district magistrate; the rest will scarcely end their careers well.
translations.idiomatic: Yang will rise at most to district magistrate; the others will scarcely come to good ends."

sentences.zh: 是時，蘇味道、王劇未知名，因調選，行儉一見，深禮異之。

translations.literal: At that time Su Weidao and Wang Ju were still unknown. When they came up for selection, Xingjian saw them once and treated them with exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao and Wang Ju were then still unknown. When they came up for selection, Xingjian saw them once and honored them with special regard.

sentences.zh: 仍謂曰：“有晚年子息，恨不見其成長。

translations.literal: He also said to them, "I have sons born late in life, and regret that I shall not see them grown."
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "I have sons born late in life, and regret that I shall not see them grown."

sentences.zh: 二公十數年當居衡石，願記識此輩。”

translations.literal: Within ten-odd years you two will hold the scales of office. I ask you to remember these men.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years or so you two will hold the highest offices of state. Remember these men for me."

sentences.zh: 其後相繼為吏部。

translations.literal: Afterward they successively served as Ministers of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In time they served in succession as Ministers of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 皆如其言。

translations.literal: All came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: All came to pass exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 行儉嚐所引偏裨，有程務挺、張虔勖、崔智辯、王方翼、黨金毗、劉敬同、郭待封、李多祚、黑齒常之，盡為名將，至刺史、將軍者數十人。

translations.literal: Among the staff officers Xingjian once promoted were Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Cui Zhibian, Wang Fangyi, Dang Jinpi, Liu Jingtong, Guo Daifeng, Li Duozuo, and Heichi Changzhi—all became famous generals, and several tens reached the rank of prefect or general.
translations.idiomatic: Among the staff officers Xingjian had promoted were Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Cui Zhibian, Wang Fangyi, Dang Jinpi, Liu Jingtong, Guo Daifeng, Li Duozuo, and Heichi Changzhi—all became famous generals, and dozens rose to prefect or general.

sentences.zh: 其所知賞，多此類也。

translations.literal: Those he recognized and rewarded were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recognized and rewarded were mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 行儉嚐令醫人合藥，請犀角、麝香，送者誤遺失，已而惶懼潛竄。

translations.literal: Xingjian once ordered a physician to compound medicine and requested rhinoceros horn and musk. The messenger who delivered them lost them by mistake and thereafter fled in secret fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian once had a physician compound medicine and requested rhinoceros horn and musk. The messenger lost them by mistake and fled in secret terror.

sentences.zh: 又有敕賜馬及新鞍，令史輒馳驟，馬倒鞍破，令史亦逃。

translations.literal: There was also an edict bestowing a horse and a new saddle. A clerk galloped it recklessly; the horse fell and the saddle broke, and the clerk also fled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also bestowed a horse and new saddle. A clerk galloped it recklessly; the horse fell and the saddle broke, and the clerk fled as well.

sentences.zh: 行儉並委所親招到，謂曰：“爾曹豈相輕耶？

translations.literal: Xingjian had his intimates summon them back and said, "Do you all look down on me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian had his intimates bring them back and said, "Do you think so little of me?"

sentences.zh: 皆錯誤耳。”

translations.literal: All were merely mistakes.
translations.idiomatic: They were all mistakes, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 待之如故。

translations.literal: He treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 初，平都支、遮匐，大獲瑰寶，蕃酋將士願觀之，行儉因宴設，遍出曆示。

translations.literal: Earlier, having pacified Duzhi and Zhefu, they obtained many rare treasures; tribal chiefs and officers wished to view them, and Xingjian, taking advantage of a banquet, brought them all out in turn for display.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Duzhi and Zhefu they had taken a great haul of rare treasures. Tribal chiefs and officers asked to see them, and Xingjian set a feast and brought everything out, item by item, for all to view.

sentences.zh: 有馬腦盤，廣二尺餘，文彩殊絕。

translations.literal: There was an agate platter more than two feet wide, its pattern and color utterly unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was an agate platter more than two feet across, its colors and patterns beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 軍吏王休烈捧盤，曆階趨進，誤躡衣，足跌便倒，盤亦隨碎，休烈驚惶，叩頭流血，行儉笑而謂曰：“爾非故也，何至於是！”

translations.literal: Army clerk Wang Xiulie carried the platter, hurrying up the steps; he accidentally trod on his robe, fell at once, and the platter shattered with him. Xiulie panicked and kowtowed until his forehead bled. Xingjian laughed and said to him, "You did not do it on purpose — why go so far!"
translations.idiomatic: Army clerk Wang Xiulie bore the platter up the steps in haste; he caught his robe, stumbled, and fell — the platter shattered with him. Xiulie was terrified and kowtowed until his forehead ran with blood. Xingjian laughed and said, "You didn't mean to — why take it so hard!"

sentences.zh: 更不形顏色。

translations.literal: He never showed it in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He never let it show on his face.

sentences.zh: 詔賜都支等資產金器皿三千餘事，駝馬稱是，並分給親故並副使已下，數日便盡。

translations.literal: An edict granted Duzhi and the others more than three thousand items of property and gold vessels, with camels and horses in proportion; all were divided among relatives, friends, and deputy envoys and below — within days it was all gone.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded Duzhi and his party more than three thousand pieces of property and gold vessels, with camels and horses to match. Xingjian divided the lot among kin, friends, and everyone down to his deputy envoys — within days it was all spent.

sentences.zh: 少子光庭，開元中為侍中，以恩例贈行儉為太尉。

translations.literal: His youngest son Guangting, during the Kaiyuan era, became chief minister; by favor he had Xingjian posthumously ennobled as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Guangting became chief minister under Kaiyuan and, by imperial favor, had Xingjian posthumously ennobled as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 光庭早孤。

translations.literal: Guangting lost his father early.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting was orphaned young.

sentences.zh: 母庫狄氏，則天時召入宮，甚見親待，光庭由是累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Kudi was summoned to court during Wu Zetian's reign and treated with great intimacy; Guangting thereby rose step by step to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Kudi, was summoned to court under Wu Zetian and treated with exceptional favor; on that account Guangting rose steadily until he reached vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後以武三思之婿緣坐，左遷郢州司馬。

translations.literal: Later, as son-in-law of Wu Sansi, he was implicated by association and demoted to secretary in E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Wu Sansi's son-in-law, he was implicated by association and demoted to secretary in Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，六遷右率府中郎將，擢授司門郎中。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, after six promotions he became a commander in the Right Leading Guard Office, then was elevated to director in the Ministry of Justice's Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, after six promotions he became a commander in the Right Leading Guard Office, then was elevated to director in the Ministry of Justice's Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: After a year more, he transferred to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he transferred to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 光庭沉靜少言，寡於交遊，既曆清要，時人初未許之。

translations.literal: Guangting was quiet and spoke little, kept few company; having passed through prestigious posts, men of the day at first did not approve of him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting was reserved and sparing of words, with few friends. He had already held prestigious posts, yet at first people did not think much of him.

sentences.zh: 及在職，公務修整，眾方歎伏焉。

translations.literal: Once in office, he put official business in good order, and only then did all admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up his duties and put official business in good order, everyone came to admire him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，將有事於岱嶽，中書令張說以大駕東巡，京師空虛，恐夷狄乘間竊發，議欲加兵守邊，以備不虞，召光庭謀兵事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when there was to be business at Mount Tai, Chief Minister Zhang Yue, because the great carriage would tour east and the capital would stand empty, feared barbarians might seize the interval and steal a rising, and proposed adding troops to guard the border against the unforeseen; he summoned Guangting to plan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as the emperor prepared the fengshan at Mount Tai, Chief Minister Zhang Yue argued that with the imperial procession touring east the capital would stand empty and barbarians might seize the moment to strike. He proposed reinforcing the frontier against surprise and summoned Guangting to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 光庭曰：“封禪者，所以告成功也。

translations.literal: Guangting said, "The fengshan is meant to announce success.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting said, "The fengshan is meant to announce success.

sentences.zh: 夫成功者，恩德無不及，百姓無不安，萬國無不懷。

translations.literal: One who succeeds — his grace reaches without exception, the hundred surnames are without unrest, and the ten thousand states are without one that does not turn toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Success means grace reaching everywhere, the people secure in all things, and every state under heaven filled with goodwill.

sentences.zh: 今將告成而懼夷狄，何以昭德也？

translations.literal: Now you are about to announce success yet fear barbarians — how may virtue be displayed?
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the eve of announcing success, you fear barbarians — how does that display virtue?

sentences.zh: 大興力役，用備不虞，且非安人也。

translations.literal: Greatly raising labor and corvée to prepare against the unforeseen — moreover this is not to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: To launch great labor and conscription to guard against surprise is hardly to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 方謀會同而阻戎心，又非懷遠也。

translations.literal: Just as you plan a gathering of all states, you would obstruct the hearts of the frontier warriors — again this is not to cherish the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Just as you plan a gathering of all states, you would chill the hearts of the frontier peoples — that is not to draw the distant near.

sentences.zh: 有此三者，則名實乖矣。

translations.literal: With these three things present, name and reality would be at odds.
translations.idiomatic: With these three things, name and reality would part.

sentences.zh: 且諸蕃之國，突厥為大，贄幣往來，願修恩好有年矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the frontier states Turk is greatest; tribute and gifts have passed back and forth for years in a wish to preserve goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the frontier states the Turks are foremost; tribute and gifts have passed back and forth for years in a wish to preserve goodwill.

sentences.zh: 今茲遣一使征其大臣赴會，必欣然應命。

translations.literal: If you now send a single envoy summoning their chief ministers to the assembly, they will surely come gladly.
translations.idiomatic: If you now send a single envoy summoning their chief ministers to the assembly, they will surely come gladly.

sentences.zh: 突厥受詔，則諸蕃君長必相率而來。

translations.literal: Once the Turks accept the edict, the frontier lords will surely follow one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turks accept the edict, the frontier lords will surely follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 雖偃旗息鼓，高枕有餘矣。”

translations.literal: Though banners be lowered and drums stilled, to pillow one's head in ease would still leave surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Even with banners lowered and drums stilled, you may rest your head on your pillow with room to spare."

sentences.zh: 說曰：“善。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Excellent.

sentences.zh: 吾所不及矣。”

translations.literal: This is beyond me."
translations.idiomatic: This is beyond me."

sentences.zh: 因奏而行之，尋轉鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He memorialized and carried it out; soon Guangting became vice minister of Rites for guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the plan and put it into effect; soon afterward Guangting was made vice minister of Rites for guest affairs.

sentences.zh: 東封還，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern fengshan, he was promoted to vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the eastern fengshan, he was promoted to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十七年，拜中書侍郎，同中書門下平章事，尋兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, co-equal under the Secretariat-Chancellery, and soon also censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, co-equal under the Secretariat-Chancellery, and soon also censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遷黃門侍郎，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of the Chancellery, still handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of the Chancellery, still handling state affairs.

sentences.zh: 從巡五陵回，拜侍中，兼吏部尚書，又加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: After accompanying the tour of the five tombs, he was made chief minister, concurrently minister of Civil Appointments, and also made a scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the tour of the five tombs, he was made chief minister, concurrently minister of Civil Appointments, and also made a scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 光庭乃撰《瑤山往則》及《維城前軌》各壹卷，上表獻之。

translations.literal: Guangting then compiled one scroll each of Guidelines from the Jade Mountain and Earlier Paths to the Rampart City and submitted them by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting then compiled one scroll each of Guidelines from the Jade Mountain and Earlier Paths to the Rampart City and submitted them by memorial.

sentences.zh: 手製褒美，賜絹五百匹，上令皇太子已下於光順門與光庭相見，以重其諷誡之意。

translations.literal: The emperor's own hand praised him and granted five hundred bolts of silk; he ordered the crown prince and those below to meet Guangting at Guangshun Gate, to honor the admonitory intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's own hand praised him and granted five hundred bolts of silk; he ordered the crown prince and those below to meet Guangting at Guangshun Gate, to honor the admonitory intent.

sentences.zh: 光庭又引壽安丞李融、拾遺張琪、著作左郎司馬利賓等，令直弘文館，撰《續春秋傳》。

translations.literal: Guangting also brought in Shou'an assistant Li Rong, remonstrance official Zhang Qi, left secretary Sima Libin, and others, assigning them to the Hongwen Institute to compile Continuations to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting also brought in Shou'an assistant Li Rong, remonstrance official Zhang Qi, left secretary Sima Libin, and others, assigning them to the Hongwen Institute to compile Continuations to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 上表請以經為禦撰，而光庭等依左氏之體為之作傳，上又手製褒賞之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the classic be treated as imperially authored while Guangting and the others would write the commentary in Zuo's style; the emperor again personally commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the classic be treated as imperially authored while Guangting and the others would write the commentary in Zuo's style; the emperor again personally commended him.

sentences.zh: 光庭委筆削於李融，書竟不就。

translations.literal: Guangting entrusted the writing to Li Rong; the book was never finished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting entrusted the writing to Li Rong; the book was never finished.

sentences.zh: 時有上書請以皇室為金德者，中書令蕭嵩奏請集百僚詳議。

translations.literal: At the time someone submitted that the imperial house should be assigned the Metal phase; Chief Minister Xiao Song memorialized to assemble the hundred officials for full deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone submitted that the imperial house should be assigned the Metal phase; Chief Minister Xiao Song memorialized to assemble the hundred officials for full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 光庭以國家符命久著史策，若有改易，恐貽後學之誚，密奏請依舊為定，乃下詔停百僚集議之事。

translations.literal: Guangting held that the dynasty's mandate had long been recorded in the histories; to change it would invite later scholars' reproach; he secretly memorialized to keep the old designation, and an edict halted the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting held that the dynasty's mandate had long been recorded in the histories; to change it would invite later scholars' reproach. He secretly memorialized to keep the old designation, and an edict halted the assembly.

sentences.zh: 二十年，扈從祠後土，加光祿大夫，封正平男。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, accompanying the sacrifice to Earth at Houtu, he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and ennobled Baron of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, accompanying the sacrifice to Earth at Houtu, he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and ennobled Baron of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年五十八，優製贈太師，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, age fifty-eight; a special edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor; court mourning three days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died, at fifty-eight; a special edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, and court was suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 初，光庭與蕭嵩爭權不協。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangting and Xiao Song had vied for power and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guangting and Xiao Song had vied for power and did not agree.

sentences.zh: 及為吏部，奏用循資格，並促選限至正月三十日令畢，其流外行署，亦令門下省之。

translations.literal: When he became minister of Civil Appointments, he memorialized use of the seniority regulations, pressing the selection deadline to the thirtieth of the first month; external placements also required Chancellery approval.
translations.idiomatic: When he became minister of Civil Appointments, he memorialized use of the seniority regulations, pressing the selection deadline to the thirtieth of the first month; external placements also required Chancellery approval.

sentences.zh: 光庭卒後，嵩又奏請一切罷之，光庭所引進者盡出為外職。

translations.literal: After Guangting died, Song again memorialized to abolish all this; Guangting's appointees were all sent to outside posts.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangting died, Song again memorialized to abolish all this; Guangting's appointees were all sent to outside posts.

sentences.zh: 時有門下主事閻麟之，為光庭腹心，專知吏部選官，每麟之裁定，光庭隨而下筆，時人語曰：“麟之口，光庭手。”

translations.literal: There was Chancellery clerk Yan Linzhi, Guangting's trusted man, solely handling Civil Appointments selections; whatever Linzhi decided, Guangting would sign — men said, "Linzhi's mouth, Guangting's hand."
translations.idiomatic: There was Chancellery clerk Yan Linzhi, Guangting's trusted man, solely handling Civil Appointments selections; whatever Linzhi decided, Guangting would sign — people said, "Linzhi's mouth, Guangting's hand."

sentences.zh: 太常博士孫琬將議光庭諡，以其用循資格，非獎勸之道，建議諡為“克”。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Sacrifices Sun Wan was about to deliberate Guangting's posthumous name; holding that seniority regulations were not the way to reward merit, he proposed the name Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Sacrifices Sun Wan was about to deliberate Guangting's posthumous name; holding that seniority regulations were not the way to reward merit, he proposed the name Ke.

sentences.zh: 時人以為希嵩意旨。

translations.literal: Men of the day thought this flattered Song's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day thought this flattered Song's wishes.

sentences.zh: 上聞而特下詔，賜諡曰忠獻，仍令中書令張九齡為其碑文。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and issued a special edict granting the posthumous name Zhongxian, ordering Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling to compose his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and issued a special edict granting the posthumous name Zhongxian, ordering Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling to compose his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 史官韋述以改諡為非，論之曰：《春秋》之義，諸侯死王事者，葬之加一等，嘉其有功而不及其賞也。

translations.literal: Historian Wei Shu held that changing the posthumous name was wrong, and argued: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when feudal lords die in the ruler's service, their burial receives one rank higher — honoring their merit without extending to the reward due them.
translations.idiomatic: Historian Wei Shu held that changing the posthumous name was wrong, and argued: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when feudal lords die in the ruler's service, their burial receives one rank higher — honoring their merit without extending to the reward due them.

sentences.zh: 爰至漢、魏，則襚之印綬，寵被窀穸，唯德是褒，豈虛授也！

translations.literal: Down through Han and Wei, grave goods included seals and cords; favor extended to the tomb — only virtue was praised. How could such titles be given in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Down through Han and Wei, grave goods included seals and cords; favor extended to the tomb — only virtue was praised. How could such titles be given in vain!

sentences.zh: 近代已來，寵贈無紀，或以職位崇顯，一切優錫；

translations.literal: In recent times honors at death know no bounds — sometimes for lofty rank everything is lavishly bestowed;
translations.idiomatic: In recent times honors at death know no bounds — sometimes for lofty rank everything is lavishly bestowed;

sentences.zh: 或以子孫榮貴，恩例所加，賢愚虛實，為一貫矣。

translations.literal: sometimes because descendants prosper, by favor's precedent — worthy and foolish, hollow and solid, treated alike.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes because descendants prosper, by favor's precedent — worthy and foolish, hollow and solid, treated alike.

sentences.zh: 裴光庭以守法之吏，驟登相位，踐曆機衡，豈不多愧？

translations.literal: Pei Guangting, as an official who kept the law, suddenly ascended to the chancellorship and trod the pivot of state — ought he not feel much shame?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting, a law-keeping clerk, suddenly reached the chancellorship and tread the scales of power — should he not feel much shame?

sentences.zh: 贈以師範，何其濫歟！

translations.literal: To grant him Grand Preceptor as teacher and model — how wanton!
translations.idiomatic: To grant him the Grand Preceptor — how excessive!

sentences.zh: 張燕公有扶翊之勳，居講諷之舊，秩躋九命，官曆二端，議者猶謂贈之過當，況光庭去斯猶遠，何妄竊之甚哉！

translations.literal: Duke Yan of Zhang had merit in supporting the throne, stood in the old office of lecturing and admonition, rank climbed to nine orders, offices passed through both ends — critics still said the posthumous gift was excessive; how much farther was Guangting from that, and how wildly did he usurp!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yan of Zhang had merit supporting the throne, long served as tutor-advisor, rank reached ninefold honors, offices spanned both ends — yet critics still called his posthumous gifts excessive. How much farther was Guangting from such standing — what gross presumption to seize such a title!

sentences.zh: 蓋名器假人，昔賢之所惋也。

translations.literal: To lend titles and insignia to the unworthy — this is what sages of old lamented.
translations.idiomatic: To lend titles and insignia to the unworthy — this is what sages of old lamented.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔晉侯選任將帥，取其說《禮》《樂》而敦《詩》《書》，良有以也。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: When the Jin ruler chose generals, he took those versed in the Rites and Music who cherished the Odes and Documents — and had good reason.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: When the Jin ruler chose generals, he took those versed in the Rites and Music who cherished the Odes and Documents — and had good reason.

sentences.zh: 夫權謀方略，兵家之大經，邦國係之以存亡，政令因之而強弱，則馮眾怙力，豨勇虎暴者，安可輕言推轂授任哉！

translations.literal: Now strategy and plotting are the great warp of the military art; states are bound to them for survival or ruin, government grows strong or weak through them — then how may one lightly speak of granting the general's baton to those who rely on the multitude and trust in force, who are pig-fierce and tiger-violent!
translations.idiomatic: Strategy and tactics are the great constant of warfare; nations live or die by them; government waxes or wanes accordingly — how then lightly grant the general's baton to those who rely on numbers and brute force, on pig-fury and tiger-violence!

sentences.zh: 故王猛、諸葛亮振起窮巷，驅駕豪傑，左指右顧，廓定霸圖，非他道也，蓋智力權變，適當其用耳。

translations.literal: Thus Wang Meng and Zhuge Liang shook off poor lanes, drove and bridled heroes, pointed left and looked right, and cleared and fixed their hegemonic designs — not by another way, but because intellect and power, adaptive change, happened to suit their use.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng and Zhuge Liang rose from poor lanes, drove heroes before them, commanded with a glance left or right, and mapped out dominion — not by another path, but because their intellect, power, and adaptive skill were exactly what the hour demanded.

sentences.zh: 劉樂城、裴聞喜，文雅方略，無謝昔賢，治戎安邊，綽有心術，儒將之雄者也。

translations.literal: Liu of Leycheng and Pei of Wenxi — in literary grace and strategy they did not yield to former worthies; in ordering armies and settling the border they abundantly had heart-craft — champions among scholar-generals.
translations.idiomatic: Liu of Leycheng and Pei of Wenxi — in culture, grace, and strategy they yield nothing to past worthies; in governing armies and securing borders they had ample craft — heroic scholar-generals.

sentences.zh: 天後預政之時，刑峻如壑，多以諛佞希恩，而樂城、甑山，昌言規正，若時無君子，安及此言？

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager anticipated government, punishments were steep as ravines; many used flattery and sycophancy to seek grace — yet Leycheng and Zengshan spoke openly to set things right; if the age had lacked gentlemen, who would have reached such words?
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager held power, punishments were deep as ravines and most sought favor through flattery — yet Leycheng and Zengshan spoke plainly to set things right; had there been no gentlemen then, who would have ventured such words?

sentences.zh: 正平銓藻吏能，文學政事，頗有深識。

translations.literal: Lord Zhengping assessed clerical talent; in letters and governance he showed real depth.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zhengping assessed clerical talent; in letters and governance he showed real depth.

sentences.zh: 而前史譏其謬諡，有涉陳壽短武侯應變之論乎！

translations.literal: Yet earlier histories mock his mistaken posthumous name — does this not touch Chen Shou's slight against the Martial Marquis on adaptability?
translations.idiomatic: Yet earlier histories mock his mistaken posthumous name — does this not touch Chen Shou's slight against the Martial Marquis on adaptability?

sentences.zh: 非通論也。

translations.literal: That is not a fair judgment.
translations.idiomatic: That is not a fair judgment.

sentences.zh: 讚曰：殷禮阿衡，周師呂尚。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Yin received his minister at the scale-beam; Zhou took Lü Shang as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Praise runs: Yin received his minister at the scale-beam; Zhou took Lü Shang as teacher.

sentences.zh: 王者之兵，儒者之將。

translations.literal: The king's armies, the Confucian generals.
translations.idiomatic: The king's weapon, the scholar's general.

sentences.zh: 樂城、聞喜，當仁不讓。

translations.literal: Leycheng and Wenxi — where benevolence stood, they did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Leycheng and Wenxi — where humanity called, they did not yield.

sentences.zh: 管、葛之譚，是吾心匠。

translations.literal: The discourse of Guan and Ge — that is the craft of my own heart.
translations.idiomatic: Talk of Guan and Ge — that is the pattern of my own mind.
